---@class OxAccountServer : OxClass
local OxAccount = lib.class('OxAccount')

function OxAccount:__index(index)
    local value = OxAccount[index] --[[@as any]]

    if type(value) == 'function' then
        self[index] = value == OxAccount.__call and function(...)
            return value(self, index, ...)
        end or function(...)
            return value(self, ...)
        end

        return self[index]
    end

    return value
end

function OxAccount:constructor(data)
    for k, v in pairs(data) do
        self[k] = v
    end
end

function OxAccount:__call(...)
    return exports.ox_core:CallAccount(self.accountId, ...)
end

function OxAccount:__tostring()
    return json.encode(self, { indent = true })
end

for method in pairs(exports.ox_core:GetAccountCalls() or {}) do
    if not rawget(OxAccount, method) then OxAccount[method] = OxAccount.__call end
end

local function CreateAccountInstance(account)
    if not account then return end

    return OxAccount:new(account)
end

local resourceName = nil

local Alert = {}

local list = {
    ['ox_lib'] = {},
    ['lt-ui'] = {},
    ['lation_ui'] = {},
}

--- Returns alert resource name.
--- @ltbridge return:list:nil
--- @ltbridge export: GetResource
function GetAlertResource()
    return resourceName
end

--- Force set alert resource.
--- Useful for config assignment.
--- @ltbridge params:list:name
--- @ltbridge export: SetResource
function SetAlertResource(name)
    ltassert(name and type(name) == 'string', 'name is required and must be a valid string')
    ltassert(list[name], 'Alert resource %s not found.', name)
    resourceName = name
    Alert = exports[name]
end

local resource = DetectResource(list, 'alert')
if resource then
    SetAlertResource(resource)
end

local adapters = {
    ['ox_lib'] = function(data)
        local result = Alert:alertDialog(data)
        return result
    end,
    ['lt-ui'] = function(data)
        local result = Alert:alertDialog(data)
        return result
    end,
    ['lation_ui'] = function(data)
        local result = Alert:alert(data)
        return result
    end,
}

--- Send alert dialog to player.
--- @param data table { header: string, content: string, centered: boolean, size = 'xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'|'xl', cancel: boolean, labels: { cancel: string, confirm: string } }
--- ```lua
--- LT.Alert.Send({
---     header = 'Alert',
---     content = 'Alert',
---     centered = true,
---     size = 'md',
---     cancel = true,
---     labels = { cancel = 'Cancel', confirm = 'Confirm' }
--- })
--- ```
--- @return 'cancel'|'confirm'|nil
--- @ltbridge export: Send
function SendAlert(data)
    local resource = GetAlertResource()
    ltassert(resource, 'alert resource not found.')
    local adapter = adapters[resource]
    return adapter(data)
end

-- Shared scene-blur leases and the reduced-motion preference. Client-only; load
-- after adapter lifecycle/shutdown and before dialog exports. No NUI/CSS blur
-- and no per-frame native calls.
UIEffects = {}

local log = Logger.create('tLib/ui-effects')
local leases, count = {}, 0
local applied, stopped = false, false
local FADE_MS = 200.0

local function supported()
    return _TLIB_IS_FIVEM and _TLIB_SIDE == 'client'
        and type(TriggerScreenblurFadeIn) == 'function'
        and type(TriggerScreenblurFadeOut) == 'function'
end

local function fadeOut(duration)
    if not applied then return end
    local ok, err = pcall(TriggerScreenblurFadeOut, duration)
    if ok and err ~= false then applied = false
    else log('Scene blur fade-out failed: ' .. tostring(err), 3) end
end

-- Internal API: acquireBlur(ownerResource?) -> opaque token, or nil on an
-- unsupported host/shutdown/native failure. Acquire only AFTER granting focus.
-- Each caller retains its token; releasing another caller's token is forbidden.
function UIEffects.acquireBlur(owner)
    if stopped or not supported() then return nil end
    if count == 0 then
        local ok, err = pcall(TriggerScreenblurFadeIn, FADE_MS)
        if not ok or err == false then
            log('Scene blur fade-in failed: ' .. tostring(err), 3)
            return nil
        end
        applied = true
    end
    local token = {}
    leases[token] = { owner = owner }
    count = count + 1
    return token
end

-- Idempotent. Only the final lease fades out, so closing a dialog cannot remove
-- blur held by a layout editor. Unknown/nil tokens do not touch global effects.
function UIEffects.releaseBlur(token)
    if token == nil or leases[token] == nil then return end
    leases[token] = nil
    count = count - 1
    if count == 0 then fadeOut(FADE_MS) end
end

Platform.onResourceStop(function(owner)
    local expired = {}
    for token, lease in pairs(leases) do
        if lease.owner == owner then expired[#expired + 1] = token end
    end
    for _, token in ipairs(expired) do UIEffects.releaseBlur(token) end
end)

Platform.onShutdown(function()
    stopped = true
    leases, count = {}, 0
    -- Finish immediately: no timer/thread can survive resource shutdown.
    fadeOut(0.0)
end)

-- Reduced motion: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` does not work in a FiveM NUI
-- — CEF always reports `no-preference` — so every such media query in this
-- estate was dead. The switch that reaches a player is the `--motion` custom
-- property on :root; every shared duration multiplies through it, so one
-- write disables all of them.
--
-- Two inputs, player over server: the server sets a house default, the player
-- states an accessibility need.
--   tlib_reduce_motion  (convar, `setr`)   server default, 0 or 1
--   tlib.motion         (KVP)              the player's own answer, if any
--
-- A consumer with its own ui_page owns its own document, so tLib cannot write
-- the property there; it publishes the answer instead, via
-- `exports.tLib:GetReduceMotion()` and the `tlib:reduceMotion` event.

local MOTION_KVP = 'tlib.motion'
local reduceMotion = false

local function readPreference()
    -- KVP first: a player who has answered has answered, and a server owner
    -- flipping the house default must not silently overrule them.
    local stored = GetResourceKvpString and GetResourceKvpString(MOTION_KVP) or nil
    if stored == 'reduce' then return true end
    if stored == 'full' then return false end
    if type(GetConvar) ~= 'function' then return false end
    return GetConvar('tlib_reduce_motion', '0') == '1'
end

local function publish()
    -- tLib's own page. `--motion: 1` is the sheet's default, so the full-motion
    -- case writes it back rather than removing the property: a consumer theme
    -- may have set it, and leaving a stale 0 behind is the failure that is hard
    -- to diagnose from inside the game.
    if type(SendNUIMessage) == 'function' then
        SendNUIMessage({ action = 'setMotion', data = { motion = reduceMotion and 0 or 1 } })
    end
    -- Platform.TriggerEvent, not the global: every other event in this tree goes
    -- through the adapter, and a bare global was the one call that did not.
    if Platform and Platform.TriggerEvent then
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tlib:reduceMotion', reduceMotion)
    end
end

--- Is motion currently reduced for this player?
function UIEffects.getReduceMotion()
    return reduceMotion
end

--- Set the player's own answer, persisted. `nil` clears it back to the convar.
function UIEffects.setReduceMotion(value)
    if value == nil then
        if DeleteResourceKvp then DeleteResourceKvp(MOTION_KVP) end
    elseif SetResourceKvp then
        SetResourceKvp(MOTION_KVP, value and 'reduce' or 'full')
    end
    reduceMotion = readPreference()
    publish()
    return reduceMotion
end

-- Guarded, matching `supported()` above and `readPreference`'s convar check.
-- This module is loaded by several Lua test hosts that provide only the blur
-- surface, and tLib's adapter is also the seam a non-FiveM platform would come
-- in through — so the motion preference degrades to an in-memory value rather
-- than taking the whole file down with it.
if Platform and Platform.wrapExport then
    Platform.wrapExport('tLib', 'GetReduceMotion', function() return reduceMotion end)
    Platform.wrapExport('tLib', 'SetReduceMotion', function(value) return UIEffects.setReduceMotion(value) end)
end

if type(RegisterCommand) == 'function' then RegisterCommand('tlibmotion', function(_, args)
    local arg = args and args[1] and tostring(args[1]):lower() or nil
    if arg == 'on' or arg == 'full' then UIEffects.setReduceMotion(false)
    elseif arg == 'off' or arg == 'reduce' then UIEffects.setReduceMotion(true)
    elseif arg == 'default' then UIEffects.setReduceMotion(nil)
    else UIEffects.setReduceMotion(not reduceMotion) end
    log(('Interface motion is now %s.'):format(reduceMotion and 'reduced' or 'full'), 1)
end, false) end

if Platform and Platform.createThread then
    Platform.createThread(function()
        reduceMotion = readPreference()
        publish()
    end)
end

local Blip = {}
Blip.__index = Blip

---@class BlipProperties
---@field label string Label of the blip
---@field coords? vector3 Coordinates of the blip
---@field entity? number Entity of the blip
---@field sprite? number Sprite of the blip
---@field color? number Color of the blip
---@field scale? number Scale of the blip
---@field shortRange? boolean|nil Whether the blip is a short range blip (default: true)
---@field display? number Display mode of the blip (default: 2)
---@field rotation? number Rotation of the blip
---@field alpha? number Alpha of the blip (default: 255)
---@field highDetail? boolean Whether the blip is a high detail blip (default: false)
---@field route? boolean Whether the blip is a route blip (default: false)
---@field routeColor? number Route color of the blip
---@field bright? boolean Whether the blip is a bright blip (default: false)
---@field flash? boolean Whether the blip is flashing (default: false)
---@field flashInterval? number Flash interval of the blip (default: 500ms)
---@field delete? fun(self: self) Delete the blip

---@type table Blip handlers
local blips = {}

local function validateCoords(coords)
    return type(coords) == 'vector3' or
        (type(coords) == 'table' and type(coords.x) == 'number' and type(coords.y) == 'number' and type(coords.z) == 'number')
end

--- Creates a new blip.
--- @param data BlipProperties Blip data
--- @return table|boolean Blip handler or false if failed
--- @ltbridge export: Create
function CreateBlip(data)
    local self = setmetatable({}, Blip)

    ltassert(data ~= nil, 'data is required')
    ltassert(type(data) == 'table', 'data must be a table')
    ltassert(data.label and type(data.label) == 'string', 'label is required and must be a valid string')
    ltassert(not (data.coords and data.entity), 'coords and entity cannot be used together')
    ltassert(data.coords or data.entity, 'coords or entity is required')

    self.type = data.coords and 'coord' or 'entity'

    if self.type == 'coord' and not validateCoords(data.coords) then
        printf('error', 'coords must be a valid vector3')
        return false
    end

    if self.type == 'entity' and (type(data.entity) ~= 'number' or not DoesEntityExist(data.entity)) then
        printf('error', 'entity must be a valid entity')
        return false
    end

    self.blip = self.type == 'entity' and AddBlipForEntity(data.entity) or
        AddBlipForCoord(data.coords.x + 0.0, data.coords.y + 0.0, data.coords.z + 0.0)

    SetBlipSprite(self.blip, data.sprite or 1)
    SetBlipScale(self.blip, (data.scale or 1.0) + 0.0)
    SetBlipColour(self.blip, data.color or 1)
    SetBlipAsShortRange(self.blip, data.shortRange ~= false)
    SetBlipDisplay(self.blip, data.display or 2)

    if data.rotation ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.rotation) == 'number', 'rotation must be a number')
        SetBlipRotation(self.blip, data.rotation)
    end
    if data.alpha ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.alpha) == 'number', 'alpha must be a number')
        ltassert(data.alpha >= 0 and data.alpha <= 255, 'alpha must be a number between 0 and 255')
        SetBlipAlpha(self.blip, data.alpha)
    end
    if data.highDetail ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.highDetail) == 'boolean', 'highDetail must be a boolean')
        SetBlipHighDetail(self.blip, data.highDetail)
    end
    if data.route ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.route) == 'boolean', 'route must be a boolean')
        SetBlipRoute(self.blip, data.route)
    end
    if data.routeColor ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.routeColor) == 'number', 'routeColor must be a number')
        SetBlipRouteColour(self.blip, data.routeColor)
    end
    if data.bright ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.bright) == 'boolean', 'bright must be a boolean')
        SetBlipBright(self.blip, data.bright)
    end
    if data.flash ~= nil then
        ltassert(type(data.flash) == 'boolean', 'flash must be a boolean')
        SetBlipFlashes(self.blip, data.flash)
        if data.flash then
            SetBlipFlashInterval(self.blip, data.flashInterval or 500)
        end
    end

    BeginTextCommandSetBlipName("STRING")
    AddTextComponentString(data.label)
    EndTextCommandSetBlipName(self.blip)

    self.index = #blips + 1
    blips[self.index] = self

    return self
end

--- Gets all blips.
--- @return table Blips
--- @ltbridge export: GetAll
function GetAllBlips()
    return blips
end

--- Deletes all blips.
--- @ltbridge export: DeleteAll
function DeleteAllBlips()
    for i = 1, #blips do
        local blip = blips[i]
        if blip then
            blip:delete()
        end
    end
end

--- Deletes the blip.
function Blip:delete()
    if DoesBlipExist(self.blip) then
        RemoveBlip(self.blip)
        blips[self.index] = nil
    end
end

--- Sets the coordinates of the blip.
--- @param coords vector3 Coordinates to set
--- @return boolean
function Blip:setCoords(coords)
    ltassert(validateCoords(coords), 'coords must be a vector3')
    ltassert(self.type == 'coord', 'blip is not a coord blip')
    SetBlipCoords(self.blip, coords.x, coords.y, coords.z)
    return true
end

--- Sets the color of the blip.
--- @param color number Color to set
--- @return boolean
function Blip:setColor(color)
    ltassert(type(color) == 'number', 'color must be a number')
    SetBlipColour(self.blip, color)
    return true
end

        end or function(...)

        end

        return self[index]

-- Player input: key binds, input blocking, input mode.

_TLIB_NUI_FOCUSED = false

-- cb is either a function, fired on eventType ('Pressed' unless 'Released' is
-- asked for), or a { press, release } pair sharing one key mapping.
local function _normalizePair(cb, eventType)
    if type(cb) == 'table' then
        return cb.press or cb.onPress or cb[1],
               cb.release or cb.onRelease or cb[2]
    end
    if eventType == 'Released' then
        return nil, cb
    end
    return cb, nil
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    -- Friendly names to the FiveM key strings RegisterKeyMapping expects. Players
    -- rebind these in Settings > Controls > FiveM.
    local _keyDefaults = {
        Up        = 'UP',
        Down      = 'DOWN',
        Left      = 'LEFT',
        Right     = 'RIGHT',
        Enter     = 'RETURN',
        BackSpace = 'BACK',
        E         = 'E',
        G         = 'G',
        H         = 'H',
        M         = 'M',
        F1        = 'F1',
        F2        = 'F2',
        F3        = 'F3',
        F5        = 'F5',
        F6        = 'F6',
        Tab       = 'TAB',
    }

    local function cmdName(resourceName, key)
        return (resourceName .. '_key_' .. key):gsub('[^%w_]', '_')
    end

    local _resourceName = GetCurrentResourceName()

    -- Per-key, so two listeners on 'Enter' get distinct command tokens.
    local _bindCount    = {}

    function Platform.bindKey(key, cb, eventType, bindingId, label)
        local pressCb, releaseCb = _normalizePair(cb, eventType)
        local token

        if type(bindingId) == 'string' and bindingId ~= '' then
            -- An explicit id is its own entry on the keybind screen, so two
            -- resources can bind the same key and both stay rebindable.
            token = bindingId:gsub('[^%w_]', '_')
        else
            local count     = (_bindCount[key] or 0) + 1
            _bindCount[key] = count
            local base      = cmdName(_resourceName, key)
            token           = count == 1 and base or (base .. '_' .. count)
        end

        -- Shown on the keybind screen; the token humanises poorly, so an
        -- explicit label is worth passing.
        local displayLabel = (type(label) == 'string' and label ~= '' and label)
            or token:gsub('_', ' ')

        -- '+token' on key-down, '-token' on key-up. Both are always registered,
        -- a missing callback as a no-op, so the engine has a matched pair.
        RegisterCommand('+' .. token, function()
            if pressCb then pressCb() end
        end, false)
        RegisterCommand('-' .. token, function()
            if releaseCb then releaseCb() end
        end, false)

        -- An unrecognised name is passed through as a FiveM one (Q, NUMPAD_8,
        -- LMENU). Falling back to an empty default instead leaves the binding
        -- unset, which breaks per-key mappings meant to work out of the box.
        local defaultKey = _keyDefaults[key] or key or ''
        RegisterKeyMapping('+' .. token, displayLabel, 'keyboard', defaultKey)
    end
else
    Platform.bindKey = Platform._stub('bindKey')
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    -- There is no single "block movement" native, so each control has to be
    -- disabled every frame for as long as blocking is on.
    Platform._blockMove = false
    Platform._blockLook = false

    local _moveControls = { 30, 31, 21, 22, 32, 44, 45, 71, 72 }
    local _lookControls = { 1, 2, 3, 4, 220, 221 }

    local _blockThreadRunning = false

    local function ensureBlockThread()
        if _blockThreadRunning then return end
        _blockThreadRunning = true
        Platform.createThread(function()
            while Platform._blockMove or Platform._blockLook do
                Platform.wait(0)
                if Platform._blockMove then
                    for _, ctrl in ipairs(_moveControls) do
                        DisableControlAction(0, ctrl, true)
                    end
                end
                if Platform._blockLook then
                    for _, ctrl in ipairs(_lookControls) do
                        DisableControlAction(0, ctrl, true)
                    end
                end
            end
            _blockThreadRunning = false
        end)
    end

    function Platform.setIgnoreMoveInput(state)
        Platform._blockMove = state == true
        if state then ensureBlockThread() end
    end

    function Platform.setIgnoreLookInput(state)
        Platform._blockLook = state == true
        if state then ensureBlockThread() end
    end
else
    Platform.setIgnoreMoveInput = Platform._stub('setIgnoreMoveInput')
    Platform.setIgnoreLookInput = Platform._stub('setIgnoreLookInput')
end

-- 1 while something owns the cursor -- tLib's own NUI focus or the pause menu.
-- Key handlers suppress input on this, so a dialog does not also drive the menu.
if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.getInputMode()
        if _TLIB_NUI_FOCUSED then return 1 end
        if IsPauseMenuActive and IsPauseMenuActive() then return 1 end
        return 0
    end
else
    Platform.getInputMode = Platform._stub('getInputMode')
end

local PlayerPedId = PlayerPedId
local PlayerId = PlayerId
local GetPlayerServerId = GetPlayerServerId
local GetVehiclePedIsIn = GetVehiclePedIsIn
local GetPedInVehicleSeat = GetPedInVehicleSeat
local GetEntityCoords = GetEntityCoords
local GetSelectedPedWeapon = GetSelectedPedWeapon
local IsEntityDead = IsEntityDead

--- @class Cache
--- @field ped number Entity ID of current player ped
--- @field playerId number Player ID
--- @field serverId number Server ID of current player
--- @field vehicle number|false Entity ID of current vehicle or false
--- @field seat number|false Seat index or false
--- @field weapon number|false Weapon hash or false
--- @field coords vector3 Current coordinates updated every 500ms
--- @field isDead boolean True if player is dead
local cache = {}
local listeners = {}

--- Get a specific cache value or the whole table.
--- @param key? 'ped'|'vehicle'|'seat'|'weapon'|'coords'|'isDead'|'playerId'|'serverId'
--- @return any
--- @ltbridge export: Get
function GetCache(key)
    if key then return cache[key] end
    return cache
end

--- Listen for changes in cache values.
--- ```lua
--- LT.Cache.OnChange('vehicle', function(vehicle, oldVehicle)
---     print('Vehicle state changed', vehicle)
--- end)
--- ```
--- @param key string The cache key to listen for ('vehicle', 'seat', 'weapon', 'isDead')
--- @param cb fun(newValue: any, oldValue: any)
--- @ltbridge export: OnChange
function OnCacheChange(key, cb)
    if not listeners[key] then listeners[key] = {} end
    table.insert(listeners[key], cb)
end

local function triggerListeners(key, newValue, oldValue)
    if not listeners[key] then return end
    for i = 1, #listeners[key] do
        listeners[key][i](newValue, oldValue)
    end
end

CreateThread(function()
    local ped = PlayerPedId()
    cache.playerId = PlayerId()
    cache.serverId = GetPlayerServerId(cache.playerId)
    cache.ped = ped
    cache.coords = GetEntityCoords(ped)
    cache.vehicle = false
    cache.seat = false
    cache.weapon = false
    cache.isDead = IsEntityDead(ped)

    while true do
        ped = PlayerPedId()

        if ped ~= cache.ped then
            local oldPed = cache.ped
            cache.ped = ped
            triggerListeners('ped', ped, oldPed)
        end

        cache.coords = GetEntityCoords(ped)

        ---@type number|false
        local vehicle = GetVehiclePedIsIn(ped, false)
        if vehicle == 0 then vehicle = false end
        
        if vehicle ~= cache.vehicle then
            local oldVehicle = cache.vehicle
            cache.vehicle = vehicle
            triggerListeners('vehicle', vehicle, oldVehicle)
        end

        if vehicle then
            ---@type number|false
            local seat = false
            for i = -1, 6 do
                if GetPedInVehicleSeat(vehicle, i) == ped then
                    seat = i
                    break
                end
            end
            if seat ~= cache.seat then
                local oldSeat = cache.seat
                cache.seat = seat
                triggerListeners('seat', seat, oldSeat)
            end
        else
            if cache.seat ~= false then
                local oldSeat = cache.seat
                cache.seat = false
                triggerListeners('seat', false, oldSeat)
            end
        end

        ---@type number|false
        local weapon = GetSelectedPedWeapon(ped)
        if weapon == `WEAPON_UNARMED` then weapon = false end
        if weapon ~= cache.weapon then
            local oldWeapon = cache.weapon
            cache.weapon = weapon
            triggerListeners('weapon', weapon, oldWeapon)
        end

        local isDead = IsEntityDead(ped)
        if isDead ~= cache.isDead then
            local oldState = cache.isDead
            cache.isDead = isDead
            triggerListeners('isDead', isDead, oldState)
        end

        Wait(500)
    end
end)

    pendingCallbacks[key] = function(response, ...)

                return p:reject(response)

        response = { response, ... }

        if p then

        end

    end

    TriggerServerEvent(cbEvent:format(event), __LT_RESOURCE_NAME, key, ...)

    if p then

            if pendingCallbacks[key] then
                pendingCallbacks[key] = nil
                p:reject(("callback '%s' timed out"):format(event))
            end
        end)

        return table.unpack(Citizen.Await(p))
    end

local log = Logger.create('tLib/adapter/world')

-- Takes either key case. A FiveM vector3 already has .x/.y/.z, so it passes
-- through without a copy.
local function _toCoordTable(v)
    if type(v) ~= 'table' and type(v) ~= 'userdata' then
        return { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 }
    end
    if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM and v.x ~= nil then
        return v
    end
    return {
        x = v.x or v.X or 0,
        y = v.y or v.Y or 0,
        z = v.z or v.Z or 0,
    }
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.getPlayerCoords()
        local coords = GetEntityCoords(PlayerPedId())
        return { x = coords.x, y = coords.y, z = coords.z }
    end
else
    Platform.getPlayerCoords = Platform._stub('getPlayerCoords')
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.getPlayerHeading()
        return GetEntityHeading(PlayerPedId())
    end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then

        -- Spins while the model loads, so call it from inside a thread.
        RequestModel(hash)
        local waited = 0
        while not HasModelLoaded(hash) do
            Citizen.Wait(10)
            waited = waited + 10
            if waited > 5000 then

        while not HasModelLoaded(hash) do
            Citizen.Wait(10)

            if waited > 5000 then
                log('createPed: model load timed out for ' .. tostring(model), 4)
                return nil
            end
        end

        local ped = CreatePed(4, hash, c.x, c.y, c.z, heading or 0,

-- Returns (player, distance), or nil, nil if nobody is within radius.
if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.getClosestPlayer(coords, radius)
        local c                    = _toCoordTable(coords)
        local myId                 = PlayerId()
        local closest, closestDist = nil, math.huge

        for _, pid in ipairs(GetActivePlayers()) do
            if pid ~= myId then
                local ped  = GetPlayerPed(pid)
                local pc   = GetEntityCoords(ped)
                local dx   = pc.x - c.x
                local dy   = pc.y - c.y
                local dz   = pc.z - c.z
                local dist = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)

                if (not radius or dist <= radius) and dist < closestDist then
                    closestDist = dist
                    closest     = pid
                end
            end
        end

        if closest then
            return closest, closestDist
        end
        return nil, nil
    end
else
    Platform.getClosestPlayer = Platform._stub('getClosestPlayer')
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.getPlayersInRadius(coords, radius)
        local c      = _toCoordTable(coords)
        local result = {}

        for _, pid in ipairs(GetActivePlayers()) do
            local ped  = GetPlayerPed(pid)
            local pc   = GetEntityCoords(ped)
            local dx   = pc.x - c.x
            local dy   = pc.y - c.y
            local dz   = pc.z - c.z
            local dist = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz)
            if dist <= radius then
                table.insert(result, pid)
            end
        end

        return result
    end
else
    Platform.getPlayersInRadius = Platform._stub('getPlayersInRadius')
end

if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    --- Ground Z at (x, y), or nil if the probe never resolves.
    function Platform.getGroundZ(x, y)
        -- GetGroundZFor_3dCoord needs a Z above the ground, so probe from high up.
        local found, groundZ = GetGroundZFor_3dCoord(x, y, 1000.0, false)
        if found then return groundZ end

        -- Nothing there yet: load the collision and retry.
        --
        -- All three coordinates, and re-requested every pass. The call used to be
        -- `RequestCollisionAtCoord(x, y)` outside the loop: the missing Z became
        -- 0.0, so the collision was requested at sea level while the probe looked
        -- down from 1000.0, and the request expires after a frame anyway -- the
        -- ten retries could poll a column that was never asked for.
        local tries = 0
        while tries < 10 do
            RequestCollisionAtCoord(x, y, 1000.0)
            Citizen.Wait(100)
            found, groundZ = GetGroundZFor_3dCoord(x, y, 1000.0, false)
            if found then return groundZ end
            tries = tries + 1
        end
        return nil
    end
else
    Platform.getGroundZ = Platform._stub('getGroundZ')
end

-- One frame of world-space text; call every frame from a thread.
-- opts: scale, color = {r,g,b,a}, outline.
if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then
    function Platform.drawText3D(coords, text, opts)
        opts          = opts or {}
        local c       = _toCoordTable(coords)
        local scale   = opts.scale or 0.35
        local color   = opts.color or { r = 255, g = 255, b = 255, a = 255 }
        local outline = opts.outline ~= false

        SetTextScale(scale, scale)
        SetTextFont(0)
        SetTextProportional(true)
        SetTextColour(color.r, color.g, color.b, color.a)
        if outline then
            SetTextOutline()
        end
        SetTextEntry('STRING')
        SetTextCentre(true)
        AddTextComponentString(tostring(text))

        local onScreen, sx, sy = World3dToScreen2d(c.x, c.y, c.z)
        if onScreen then
            DrawText(sx, sy)
        end
    end
else
    Platform.drawText3D = Platform._stub('drawText3D')
end

-- One frame of a marker; call every frame from a thread.
-- opts: dir, rot, scale, color, bobUpDown, faceCamera.
if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then

        opts      = opts or {}

            markerType,
            c.x, c.y, c.z,
            dir.x, dir.y, dir.z,
            rot.x, rot.y, rot.z,
            scl.x, scl.y, scl.z,
            col.r, col.g, col.b, col.a,

    end

end

function lib.filter(string, ...)

    local result = string
    local filters = {...}

    for _, filter in ipairs(filters) do
        if type(filter) == 'string' then
            result = result:gsub(filter, '')
        elseif type(filter) == 'table' then
            local pattern = filter[1]
            local targetIndex = filter[2]
            local count = 0

            result = result:gsub(pattern, function(match)
                count = count + 1
                if count == targetIndex then
                    return ''
                end
                return match
            end)
        end
    end

    return result
end

    text     = true,
    number   = true,
    password = true,

    dropdown = true,

    local opts = {}
    if type(f.options) == 'table' then
        for _, opt in ipairs(f.options) do
            if type(opt) == 'table' and type(opt.value) == 'string' and type(opt.label) == 'string' then

    local fieldType = type(f.type) == 'string' and f.type or 'text'

        log('serialiseField: unknown type "' .. tostring(f.type) .. '", defaulting to "text"', 3)
        fieldType = 'text'
    end

    local id = type(f.id) == 'string' and f.id ~= '' and f.id
    if not id then
        log('serialiseField: field is missing a string id — skipping', 3)
        return nil
    end

    local s = {
        id          = id,
        type        = fieldType,
        label       = type(f.label) == 'string' and f.label or '',
        description = type(f.description) == 'string' and f.description or nil,
        required    = f.required == true,
        disabled    = f.disabled == true,
        section     = type(f.section) == 'string' and f.section or nil,
        row         = type(f.row) == 'string' and f.row or nil,
        flex        = type(f.flex) == 'string' and f.flex or nil,
        tab         = type(f.tab) == 'string' and f.tab or nil,
    }

    if fieldType == 'text' or fieldType == 'number' or
        fieldType == 'password' or fieldType == 'textarea' then
        s.placeholder  = type(f.placeholder) == 'string' and f.placeholder or nil
        s.defaultValue = type(f.defaultValue) == 'string' and f.defaultValue or nil
        -- Enforced on the page too, not only the server: this serialiser is a
        -- whitelist, so an unnamed cap never reaches the page — once let a
        -- player's over-limit submission through to a silent server drop.
        s.maxLength    = type(f.maxLength) == 'number' and f.maxLength > 0
            and math.floor(f.maxLength) or nil
        if fieldType == 'number' then
            s.min = type(f.min) == 'number' and f.min or nil
            s.max = type(f.max) == 'number' and f.max or nil
        end
        if fieldType == 'textarea' then
            -- Was hard-coded to 3 with no way through; tRadar's manual chapters
            -- run 20-40 lines, rendered in a ~90px box inside an xl dialog with
            -- a 360px panel floor.
            s.rows = type(f.rows) == 'number' and f.rows >= 1
                and math.min(math.floor(f.rows), 40) or nil
        end
    elseif fieldType == 'dropdown' or fieldType == 'select' or fieldType == 'radio' then
        s.options      = validateOptions(f)
        s.placeholder  = type(f.placeholder) == 'string' and f.placeholder or nil
        s.defaultValue = type(f.defaultValue) == 'string' and f.defaultValue or nil
    elseif fieldType == 'slider' then
        s.min          = type(f.min) == 'number' and f.min or 0
        s.max          = type(f.max) == 'number' and f.max or 100
        s.step         = type(f.step) == 'number' and f.step or 1
        s.defaultValue = type(f.defaultValue) == 'number' and f.defaultValue or s.min
    elseif fieldType == 'checkbox' then
        s.defaultValue = f.defaultValue == true
    elseif fieldType == 'button' then
        s.variant = type(f.variant) == 'string' and f.variant or 'default'
        -- The confirmation question. `variant = 'destructive'` is colour only, so
        -- a delete button looked dangerous but was still one click from firing.
        -- Bounded at 512, same key and meaning as a menu row's `confirm`,
        -- rendering the same two buttons on both surfaces. An empty string means
        -- nil, not a question with no text.
        s.confirm = type(f.confirm) == 'string' and f.confirm ~= ''
            and #f.confirm <= 512 and f.confirm or nil
    end

    return s
end

--- Authoring mistakes in a spec, as sentences. Spec content drifts where no stylesheet
--- reaches: tLS shipped three `variant = 'primary'` buttons beside the footer's own and no
--- descriptions at all. Meant for the person writing the spec, so it is logged at DEBUG at the
--- one place a spec is in hand, and never shown to a player: it used to run in the player's
--- NUI on every open of every dialog, for faults only the author can fix.
local function specWarnings(fields)
    local primaries, undescribed = {}, {}
    for _, field in ipairs(fields) do
        if field.type == 'button' then
            if field.variant == 'primary' then primaries[#primaries + 1] = field.id end
            if field.description == nil or field.description == '' then
                undescribed[#undescribed + 1] = field.id
            end
        end
    end

    local warnings = {}
    -- The footer's submit is already primary, so a primary FIELD competes with it.
    if #primaries > 1 then
        warnings[#warnings + 1] = ('%d fields declare variant "primary" (%s). The footer submit '
            .. 'button is already the primary action, so these compete with it and with each '
            .. 'other: leave one, or none.'):format(#primaries, table.concat(primaries, ', '))
    end
    if #undescribed > 0 then
        warnings[#warnings + 1] = ('button field(s) with no description: %s. A button in a settings '
            .. 'dialog changes something; say what.'):format(table.concat(undescribed, ', '))
    end
    return warnings
end

local function serialiseDialog(id, opts)
    local fields = {}
    if type(opts.fields) == 'table' then
        for _, f in ipairs(opts.fields) do
            local sf = serialiseField(f)
            if sf then table.insert(fields, sf) end
        end
    end

    local size = type(opts.size) == 'string' and opts.size or 'md'
    if size ~= 'sm' and size ~= 'md' and size ~= 'lg' and size ~= 'xl' then size = 'md' end

    -- When omitted while fields declare `tab`, the page derives tabs from
    -- first-occurrence order with id == label.
    local tabs = nil
    if type(opts.tabs) == 'table' then
        tabs = {}
        for _, t in ipairs(opts.tabs) do
            if type(t) == 'table' and type(t.id) == 'string' and t.id ~= '' then
                -- `view` names a built-in panel the page renders in place of this
                -- tab's fields (`DialogTab.view`). Once missing from this
                -- serialiser, so a `view` tab reached the page as an ordinary
                -- content tab and drew an empty panel — the tab was there, the
                -- browser was not. Whitelisted, not passed through: an unknown
                -- view falls into the same blank panel.
                local view = t.view == 'marketplace' and t.view or nil
                if t.view ~= nil and not view then
                    log('ShowDialog: tab "' .. t.id .. '" has unknown view "' ..
                        tostring(t.view) .. '" -- rendering its fields instead', 3)
                end
                table.insert(tabs, {
                    id        = t.id,
                    label     = type(t.label) == 'string' and t.label or t.id,
                    icon      = type(t.icon) == 'string' and t.icon or nil,
                    action    = t.action == true or nil,
                    separator = t.separator == true or nil,
                    view      = view,
                })
            end
        end
        if #tabs == 0 then tabs = nil end
    end

    return {
        id          = id,
        title       = type(opts.title) == 'string' and opts.title or 'Dialog',
        description = type(opts.description) == 'string' and opts.description or nil,
        fields      = fields,
        tabs        = tabs,
        submitLabel = type(opts.submitLabel) == 'string' and opts.submitLabel or nil,
        cancelLabel = type(opts.cancelLabel) == 'string' and opts.cancelLabel or nil,
        size        = size,
        -- Opt out of "reopen where you left it": the page remembers the active
        -- tab, scroll offsets and drag position per dialog id, so a dialog
        -- closing for a detour comes back where it was. `resetState = true`
        -- forces a first-run dialog instead. Sent only when true, on the same
        -- whitelist discipline as `view` above.
        resetState  = opts.resetState == true or nil,
        blur        = opts.blur ~= false,
        theme       = (type(opts.theme) == 'string' and opts.theme ~= '') and opts.theme or nil,
    }
end

-- Taking NUI focus is a one-way door: only the dialog's submit/cancel callbacks
-- lead back to unlockPlayerInput, and a page that never loads (a source-archive
-- build ships UI assets that 404) locks the player out until they reconnect.
-- Hence two guards, both inert for a healthy dialog: focus is deferred behind
-- the onNUIReady handshake, and a watchdog covers the page mounting then dying.

-- Long enough to absorb a cold disk or a heavy join; the bundle normally readies
-- within a second of resource start.
local NUI_READY_TIMEOUT_MS  = 15000

-- Idle time, not lifetime: every dialogChange resets it and the UI emits one per
-- field edit, so this only elapses for a dead page or an AFK player. Shorter risks
-- yanking the cursor from someone still reading.
local FOCUS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000

local _focusWatchdog = nil
local _focusDialogId = nil
local _readyWatchdog = nil
local _readyWarned   = false
local _blurLease     = nil
local _activeDialogId = nil
local _activeOwner    = nil
local _stopped        = false
local _instanceSerial = 0
local _usedIds = {}
local _stoppingOwners = {}

-- Native focus may still be false while a dialog waits in the NUI-ready queue, so
-- other tLib editors check this rather than the focus flag.
function DialogExports.isActive()
    return not _stopped and _activeDialogId ~= nil
end

local function callable(value)
    if type(value) == 'function' then return true end
    local kind = type(value)
    if kind ~= 'table' and kind ~= 'userdata' then return false end
    local mt = getmetatable(value)
    return type(mt) == 'table' and type(mt.__call) == 'function'
end

local function invoke(callback, ...)
    if not callback then return end
    local ok, err = pcall(callback, ...)
    if not ok then log('Dialog callback failed: ' .. tostring(err), 4) end
end

local function ownedEntry(id)
    local entry = DialogState.get(id)
    if entry and entry.owner == Platform.getInvokingResource() then return entry end
end

-- Tokenless replies work for an id's first lifetime only: once reused, an id alone
-- cannot tell an old browser response from a new one.
local function replyEntry(data)
    if type(data) ~= 'table' or type(data.id) ~= 'string' then return nil end
    local entry = DialogState.get(data.id)
    if not entry or _activeDialogId ~= data.id then return nil end
    if data.instance ~= entry.instance
        and not (data.instance == nil and entry.allowLegacyReply) then return nil end
    return entry
end

local function findField(entry, id)
    if type(id) ~= 'string' then return nil end
    for _, field in ipairs(entry.schema.fields) do
        if field.id == id then return field end
    end
end

local function validValue(field, value)
    if field.disabled or field.type == 'button' then return false end
    if field.type == 'checkbox' then return type(value) == 'boolean' end
    if field.type == 'slider' then
        return type(value) == 'number' and value == value and math.abs(value) < math.huge
            and value >= field.min and value <= field.max
    end
    if type(value) ~= 'string' then return false end
    if field.type == 'number' then
        if value == '' and not field.required then return true end
        local n = tonumber(value)
        return n ~= nil and n == n and math.abs(n) < math.huge
            and (not field.min or n >= field.min) and (not field.max or n <= field.max)
    end
    if field.type == 'select' or field.type == 'dropdown' or field.type == 'radio' then
        for _, option in ipairs(field.options) do if option.value == value then return true end end
        return value == '' and not field.required
    end
    return true
end

local function releaseDialogBlur()
    UIEffects.releaseBlur(_blurLease)
    _blurLease = nil
end

local function cancelFocusWatchdog()
    if _focusWatchdog then
        Platform.clearTimeout(_focusWatchdog)
        _focusWatchdog = nil
    end
    _focusDialogId = nil
end

-- NUI focus is a process-wide switch, so a rescue path calling SetNuiFocus(false)
-- blindly could yank the cursor from an unrelated resource's UI. Rescue paths
-- release only what tLib took; the normal close paths stay unconditional.
local function tlibHoldsFocus()
    return _TLIB_NUI_FOCUSED == true or _TLIB_UI_FOCUSED == true
end

local function lockPlayerInput()
    Platform.setIgnoreMoveInput(true)
    Platform.setIgnoreLookInput(true)
end

local function unlockPlayerInput(ui, id)
    -- Late callbacks/CloseDialog for a replaced dialog must not unlock its successor.
    if id and id ~= _activeDialogId then return end
    _activeDialogId, _activeOwner = nil, nil
    releaseDialogBlur()
    -- Every route that gives input back runs through here, so this is the only
    -- place the watchdog needs standing down.
    cancelFocusWatchdog()
    Platform.setInputMode(ui, 0)
    Platform.setIgnoreMoveInput(false)
    Platform.setIgnoreLookInput(false)
end

local _dialogCallbacks = {}

-- Shared teardown for CloseDialog and the focus watchdog. A rescue reports itself
-- as a cancel rather than inventing a third outcome consumers do not handle.
local function closeDialog(ui, id)
    local entry = DialogState.get(id)
    if not entry then return end
    local cbs = _dialogCallbacks[id]
    _dialogCallbacks[id] = nil
    DialogState.remove(id)
    Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'closeDialog', { id = id, instance = entry.instance })
    unlockPlayerInput(ui, id)
    Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:cancelled', id)
    if cbs and cbs.onCancel then
        invoke(cbs.onCancel)
    end
end

-- Armed when focus is granted, cancelled by unlockPlayerInput on every normal
-- close, so it only fires once the page has stopped talking to us entirely.
local function armFocusWatchdog(ui, id)
    cancelFocusWatchdog()
    _focusDialogId = id
    _focusWatchdog = Platform.setTimeout(function()
        _focusWatchdog = nil
        _focusDialogId = nil
        -- Submitted, cancelled or closed in the meantime: nothing is held.
        if not DialogState.get(id) then return end
        log('Dialog "' .. tostring(id) .. '" has held input focus for '
            .. tostring(math.floor(FOCUS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000)) .. 's without a single message from the '
            .. 'NUI page. Assuming the page stopped responding and closing the dialog so the '
            .. 'player is not left locked out of their controls.', 3)
        closeDialog(ui, id)
    end, FOCUS_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS)
end

-- A no-op unless a watchdog is already armed for this exact dialog: a stray event
-- must not arm one, or a dialog that never took focus would get a timer that
-- closes it.
local function refreshFocusWatchdog(ui, id)
    if _focusWatchdog and _focusDialogId == id then
        armFocusWatchdog(ui, id)
    end
end

-- Focus is gated on the ready handshake, so nothing is locked in this case. This
-- exists to turn "the command silently does nothing" into a line naming the cause.
local function armNuiReadyWatchdog(ui)
    if _readyWatchdog or _readyWarned then return end
    _readyWatchdog = Platform.setTimeout(function()
        _readyWatchdog = nil
        if Platform.isNUIReady() then return end
        _readyWarned = true
        log('A dialog was requested but tLib\'s NUI page has not reported ready after '
            .. tostring(math.floor(NUI_READY_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000)) .. 's, so no dialog can be shown. This is '
            .. 'almost always missing UI assets: tLib/client/ui/assets/ is excluded by .gitignore, so a '
            .. 'copy taken from the source archive ships an index.html whose script tag 404s and '
            .. 'the page never mounts. Install the packaged release (tLib.zip) instead of a source '
            .. 'download, or build the UI from the tLib folder. Player input has been left with '
            .. 'the game, so nobody is locked out.', 4)
        -- In case some other path grabbed focus first.
        if tlibHoldsFocus() then unlockPlayerInput(ui) end
    end, NUI_READY_TIMEOUT_MS)
end

-- Never grants focus before the page confirms it is listening, because only the
-- page can give it back.
local function acquireFocus(ui, id)
    local entry = DialogState.get(id)
    if not Platform.isNUIReady() then
        armNuiReadyWatchdog(ui)
    end
    Platform.onNUIReady(function()
        -- CloseDialog may have run while the page was still loading.
        if _stopped or _activeDialogId ~= id or DialogState.get(id) ~= entry then return end
        Platform.setInputMode(ui, 1)
        lockPlayerInput()
        -- Acquire before releasing to avoid a flash between blurred dialogs.
        local previous = _blurLease
        _blurLease = entry.schema.blur and UIEffects.acquireBlur(_activeOwner) or nil
        UIEffects.releaseBlur(previous)
        armFocusWatchdog(ui, id)
    end)
end

local function wireEvents(ui)
    Platform.onUIEvent(ui, 'dialogSubmit', function(data)
        local entry = replyEntry(data)
        if not entry or type(data.values) ~= 'table' then return end
        local values = {}
        for id, value in pairs(data.values) do
            local field = findField(entry, id)
            if not field then return end
            -- Disabled fields may be echoed by the renderer but cannot be changed.
            if not field.disabled then
                if not validValue(field, value) then return end
                values[id] = value
            end
        end
        for _, field in ipairs(entry.schema.fields) do
            if field.required and not field.disabled and field.type ~= 'button'
                and (values[field.id] == nil or values[field.id] == '') then return end
        end
        local cbs                 = _dialogCallbacks[data.id]
        _dialogCallbacks[data.id] = nil
        DialogState.remove(data.id)
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'closeDialog', { id = data.id, instance = entry.instance })
        unlockPlayerInput(ui, data.id)
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:submitted', data.id, values)
        if cbs and cbs.onSubmit then
            invoke(cbs.onSubmit, values)
        end
    end)

    Platform.onUIEvent(ui, 'dialogChange', function(data)
        local entry = replyEntry(data)
        if not entry then return end
        local field = findField(entry, data.fieldId)
        if not field or not validValue(field, data.value) then return end
        refreshFocusWatchdog(ui, data.id)
        local cbs = _dialogCallbacks[data.id]
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:changed', data.id, data.fieldId, data.value)
        if DialogState.get(data.id) == entry and cbs then
            invoke(cbs.onChange, data.fieldId, data.value)
        end
    end)

    Platform.onUIEvent(ui, 'dialogButtonClick', function(data)
        local entry = replyEntry(data)
        if not entry then return end
        local field = findField(entry, data.fieldId)
        local allowed = field and field.type == 'button' and not field.disabled
        if not field and type(data.fieldId) == 'string' then
            for _, tab in ipairs(entry.schema.tabs or {}) do
                if tab.id == data.fieldId and tab.action then allowed = true end
            end
        end
        if not allowed then return end
        refreshFocusWatchdog(ui, data.id)
        local cbs = _dialogCallbacks[data.id]
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:buttonClick', data.id, data.fieldId)
        if DialogState.get(data.id) == entry and cbs then
            invoke(cbs.onButtonClick, data.fieldId)
        end
    end)

    Platform.onUIEvent(ui, 'dialogCancel', function(data)
        if not replyEntry(data) then return end
        local cbs = _dialogCallbacks[data.id]
        _dialogCallbacks[data.id] = nil
        DialogState.remove(data.id)
        unlockPlayerInput(ui, data.id)
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:cancelled', data.id)
        if cbs and cbs.onCancel then
            invoke(cbs.onCancel)
        end
    end)
end

function DialogExports.register()
    local ui = DialogState.getUI()
    wireEvents(ui)

    Platform.onResourceStop(function(owner)
        _stoppingOwners[owner] = true
        if not _stopped and _activeDialogId and _activeOwner == owner then
            closeDialog(ui, _activeDialogId)
        end
        _stoppingOwners[owner] = nil
    end)
    Platform.onShutdown(function()
        _stopped = true
        if _readyWatchdog then
            Platform.clearTimeout(_readyWatchdog)
            _readyWatchdog = nil
        end
        if _activeDialogId then closeDialog(ui, _activeDialogId) end
        unlockPlayerInput(ui)
        _dialogCallbacks = {}
    end)

    local function registerExport(name, fn)
        Platform.export('tLib', name, fn)
    end

    -- Returns the resolved dialog id, generating one when `id` is nil.
    --
    -- Results arrive both as local events (tLib:dialog:submitted/cancelled) and
    -- through inline callbacks, which are additive rather than a replacement.
    -- onSubmit/onCancel may be passed positionally for backward compatibility, or on
    -- opts alongside onChange and onButtonClick.
    registerExport('ShowDialog', function(id, opts, onSubmit, onCancel)
        if _stopped then return nil end
        if HudLayout and HudLayout.isEditing() then return nil, 'HUD editor is open' end
        if type(opts) ~= 'table' then
            log('ShowDialog: opts must be a table', 4)
            return nil
        end

        if opts.blur ~= nil and type(opts.blur) ~= 'boolean' then
            return nil, 'Dialog blur must be a boolean'
        end

        if opts.resetState ~= nil and type(opts.resetState) ~= 'boolean' then
            return nil, 'Dialog resetState must be a boolean'
        end

        id = (type(id) == 'string' and id ~= '') and id or DialogState.generateId()

        local owner = Platform.getInvokingResource()
        if owner and _stoppingOwners[owner] then return nil, 'Dialog owner is stopping' end
        if DialogState.get(id) and not ownedEntry(id) then return nil, 'Dialog belongs to another resource' end
        local cbs = {
            onSubmit = onSubmit or opts.onSubmit,
            onCancel = onCancel or opts.onCancel,
            onChange = opts.onChange,
            onButtonClick = opts.onButtonClick,
        }
        for _, cb in pairs(cbs) do
            if not callable(cb) then return nil, 'Dialog callback must be callable' end
        end
        local serialised = serialiseDialog(id, opts)
        for _, warning in ipairs(specWarnings(serialised.fields)) do
            log(('dialog "%s": %s'):format(id, warning), 1)
        end
        local seen = {}
        for _, field in ipairs(serialised.fields) do
            if seen[field.id] then return nil, 'Duplicate dialog field id' end
            seen[field.id] = true
        end
        local previousId = _activeDialogId
        local previous = previousId and DialogState.get(previousId)
        local previousCallbacks = previousId and _dialogCallbacks[previousId]
        if previousId then
            _dialogCallbacks[previousId] = nil
            DialogState.remove(previousId)
        end
        cancelFocusWatchdog()
        _instanceSerial = _instanceSerial + 1
        serialised.instance = _instanceSerial
        DialogState.register(id, serialised)
        local entry = DialogState.get(id)
        entry.owner, entry.instance = owner, _instanceSerial
        entry.allowLegacyReply = not _usedIds[id]
        _usedIds[id] = true
        _dialogCallbacks[id] = cbs
        _activeDialogId, _activeOwner = id, owner

        -- Install the successor before notification: a reentrant ShowDialog is
        -- newer and wins. Never let this outer call overwrite or focus it later.
        if previous then
            Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'closeDialog', { id = previousId, instance = previous.instance })
            Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:cancelled', previousId)
            if previousCallbacks then invoke(previousCallbacks.onCancel) end
        end
        if _stopped or DialogState.get(id) ~= entry or _activeDialogId ~= id then
            return nil, 'Dialog superseded during replacement'
        end
        Platform.bringUIToFront(ui)
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'showDialog', serialised)
        -- sendUIEvent buffers on the same signal and the adapter flushes it before
        -- running ready callbacks, so the dialog is on screen before focus is taken.
        acquireFocus(ui, id)
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:dialog:opened', id)
        return id
    end)

    -- Merge properties into one field of an open dialog, for cases like filling
    -- select options after an async lookup.
    registerExport('UpdateDialogField', function(dialogId, fieldId, updates)
        if type(dialogId) ~= 'string' or dialogId == '' then
            log('UpdateDialogField: dialogId must be a non-empty string', 3)
            return
        end
        if type(fieldId) ~= 'string' or fieldId == '' then
            log('UpdateDialogField: fieldId must be a non-empty string', 3)
            return
        end
        if type(updates) ~= 'table' then
            log('UpdateDialogField: updates must be a table', 3)
            return
        end
        if not ownedEntry(dialogId) then
            log('UpdateDialogField: dialog "' .. dialogId .. '" is not open', 1)
            return
        end

        local entry = ownedEntry(dialogId)
        local field = findField(entry, fieldId)
        if not field then return end
        -- Patches update the validation schema as well as the page.
        local payload = { dialogId = dialogId, fieldId = fieldId, instance = entry.instance }
        if updates.options and type(updates.options) == 'table' then
            local opts = {}
            for _, opt in ipairs(updates.options) do
                if type(opt) == 'table' and type(opt.value) == 'string' and type(opt.label) == 'string' then
                    table.insert(opts, { value = opt.value, label = opt.label })
                end
            end
            payload.options = opts
        end
        if updates.defaultValue ~= nil then
            local candidate = {}
            for key, value in pairs(field) do candidate[key] = value end
            candidate.disabled = false
            candidate.options = payload.options or candidate.options
            if not validValue(candidate, updates.defaultValue) then return end
            payload.defaultValue = updates.defaultValue
        end
        if updates.disabled ~= nil then
            payload.disabled = updates.disabled == true
        end
        if type(updates.label) == 'string' then payload.label = updates.label end
        if field.type == 'button' and (updates.variant == 'default'
            or updates.variant == 'primary' or updates.variant == 'destructive') then
            payload.variant = updates.variant
        end
        for key, value in pairs(payload) do
            if key ~= 'dialogId' and key ~= 'fieldId' and key ~= 'instance' then field[key] = value end
        end
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'updateDialogField', payload)
    end)

    -- Replaces the fields array without recreating the dialog. Existing values are
    -- preserved; new fields get their defaultValue.
    registerExport('UpdateDialogFields', function(dialogId, fields)
        if type(dialogId) ~= 'string' or dialogId == '' then
            log('UpdateDialogFields: dialogId must be a non-empty string', 3)
            return
        end
        if type(fields) ~= 'table' then
            log('UpdateDialogFields: fields must be a table', 3)
            return
        end
        if not ownedEntry(dialogId) then
            log('UpdateDialogFields: dialog "' .. dialogId .. '" is not open', 1)
            return
        end
        local serialised, seen = {}, {}
        for _, f in ipairs(fields) do
            local sf = serialiseField(f)
            if sf then
                if seen[sf.id] then return end
                seen[sf.id] = true
                table.insert(serialised, sf)

        if type(id) ~= 'string' or id == '' then

        closeDialog(ui, id)
    end)

  assert(resource, ('resourceName is required, got %s'):format(resource))

    end
  end

  return metadata
end

function lib.closestEntity(inputCoords, radialDistance, pools, excludes)
  assert(inputCoords == nil or type(inputCoords) == "table", ("inputCoords must be a table, got %s"):format(type(inputCoords)))
  assert(type(radialDistance) == "number", ("radialDistance must be a number, got %s"):format(type(radialDistance)))
  assert(type(pools) == "table", ("pools must be a string, got %s"):format(type(pools)))
  assert(excludes == nil or type(excludes) == "table", ("excludes must be a table, got %s"):format(type(excludes)))

  local inputVec = type(inputCoords.x) == 'number' and vec3(inputCoords.x, inputCoords.y, inputCoords.z) or inputCoords

  local gamePools
  for i = 1, #pools do
    gamePools[#gamePools + 1] = GetGamePool(('C%s'):format(pools[i]))
  end

  local closestEntity = nil
  local closestDistance = radialDistance

  local excludeMap
  if excludes then
    excludeMap = {}
    for i = 1, #excludes do
      excludeMap[excludes[i]] = true
    end
  end

  for currentPool = 1, #gamePools do
    local entities <const> = gamePools[currentPool]

    for currentEntity = 1, #entities do
      local entity <const> = entities[currentEntity]

      if excludeMap and excludeMap[entity] then
        goto continue
      end

      local entityCoords <const> = GetEntityCoords(entity)
      local distance <const> = #(inputVec - entityCoords)

      if distance < closestDistance then
        closestDistance = distance
        closestEntity = entity
      end

      ::continue::
    end
  end

  return closestEntity, closestDistance
end

--- Creates a new OOP class.
--- @param name string Class name.
--- @param super? table Parent class to inherit from.
--- @return table
--- @ltbridge export: Create
function CreateClass(name, super)
    local cls = {}
    cls.__name = name
    cls.__index = cls
    cls.super = super

    if super then
        setmetatable(cls, { __index = super })
    end

    function cls.new(...)
        local instance = setmetatable({}, cls)
        instance.__destroyed = false
        
        if instance.constructor then
            instance:constructor(...)
        end
        return instance
    end

    function cls:include(mixin)
        for k, v in pairs(mixin) do
            if k ~= 'constructor' and k ~= '__index' and k ~= 'super' and k ~= '__name' then
                cls[k] = v
            end
        end
        return cls
    end

    function cls:isA(other)
        local current = self
        while current do
            if current == other then return true end
            
            local mt = getmetatable(current)
            if mt and mt.__index and mt.__index == other then return true end
            
            current = current.super
        end
        return false
    end

    local privateScope = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
    function cls:private()
        local p = privateScope[self]
        if not p then
            p = {}
            privateScope[self] = p
        end
        return p
    end

    function cls:destroy()
        if self.__destroyed then return end
        self.__destroyed = true
        
        if self.destructor then
            self:destructor()
        end
    end

    return cls
end

-- Shared HUD layout data. No natives or renderer state belong in this module.
HudLayoutSchema = {}
local S = HudLayoutSchema
local anchors = { ['top-left'] = true, ['top-right'] = true, ['bottom-left'] = true,
    ['bottom-right'] = true, center = true }

-- Offsets are a ratio of a 1080px-tall reference screen -- the same unit the
-- widget's own size scales by -- so a corner inset stays visually constant from
-- 16:9 to 32:9. Centre-anchored X stays proportional to width. Mirrored by its
-- TypeScript counterpart; the two must agree or the editor and the game disagree.
S.REFERENCE_HEIGHT = 1080
S.MAX_OFFSET = 4
S.MIN_VISIBLE_PIXELS = 96
S.MIN_VISIBLE_FRACTION = 0.4

function S.finite(value, min, max)
    return type(value) == 'number' and value == value and value >= min and value <= max
end
function S.id(value)
    return type(value) == 'string' and #value > 0 and #value <= 80 and value:match('^[%w_-]+$') ~= nil
end
function S.copy(layout)
    return { x = layout.x, y = layout.y, scale = layout.scale, visible = layout.visible, anchor = layout.anchor }
end
function S.layout(value, component)
    if type(value) ~= 'table' or not anchors[value.anchor]
        or not S.finite(value.x, -S.MAX_OFFSET, S.MAX_OFFSET)
        or not S.finite(value.y, -S.MAX_OFFSET, S.MAX_OFFSET)
        or not S.finite(value.scale, component.minScale, component.maxScale)
        or type(value.visible) ~= 'boolean' then return nil end
    if not component.canHide and not value.visible then return nil end
    if not component.canScale and value.scale ~= component.defaults.scale then return nil end
    return S.copy(value)
end
-- Recoverability constraint, shared with the TypeScript mirror. Applies to
-- every component: a widget must always be grabbable again, whatever put it
-- where it is -- a drag, a resolution change, or a record written by an
-- older version.
-- Pixels are CSS pixels at the given viewport; fraction uses the rendered extent.
function S.constrain(layout, component, viewport)
    if type(viewport) ~= 'table' or not S.finite(viewport.width, 1, 16384)
        or not S.finite(viewport.height, 1, 16384) then return nil end
    local px = component.minVisiblePixels or S.MIN_VISIBLE_PIXELS
    local fraction = component.minVisibleFraction or S.MIN_VISIBLE_FRACTION
    local pivotX = layout.anchor == 'center' and 0.5 or (layout.anchor:find('right') and 1 or 0)
    local pivotY = layout.anchor == 'center' and 0.5 or (layout.anchor:find('bottom') and 1 or 0)
    -- One unit of x/y is a reference height, except centre-anchored x (see above).
    local unitX = layout.anchor == 'center' and viewport.width or viewport.height
    local unitY = viewport.height
    local function axis(size, unit, extent, pivot, offset)
        local need = math.min(extent, size, math.max(px, extent * fraction))
        local base = pivot * (size - extent)
        local start = base + offset * unit
        local clamped = math.max(need - extent, math.min(size - need, start))
        -- An already-legal placement is returned verbatim. Round-tripping it
        -- through the pixel conversion would rewrite saved values by a float
        -- epsilon every time a component registered.
        if clamped == start then return offset end
        return math.max(-S.MAX_OFFSET, math.min(S.MAX_OFFSET, (clamped - base) / unit))
    end
    local result = S.copy(layout)
    local scale = layout.scale * viewport.height / S.REFERENCE_HEIGHT
    result.x = axis(viewport.width, unitX, component.width * scale, pivotX, layout.x)
    result.y = axis(viewport.height, unitY, component.height * scale, pivotY, layout.y)
    return result
end
-- v1 stored x as a fraction of viewport WIDTH. Convert assuming the record was
-- saved at 16:9, which is right for effectively every existing save; Reset
-- recovers the rest. Centre-anchored x was already proportional to width.
function S.migrate(layout)
    if type(layout) ~= 'table' or type(layout.anchor) ~= 'string' or layout.anchor == 'center' then return layout end
    if not S.finite(layout.x, -S.MAX_OFFSET, S.MAX_OFFSET) then return layout end
    local result = S.copy(layout)
    result.x = math.max(-S.MAX_OFFSET, math.min(S.MAX_OFFSET, layout.x * (16 / 9)))
    return result
end
function S.component(owner, id, options)
    if not S.id(owner) or not S.id(id) or type(options) ~= 'table' then return nil end
    if type(options.label) ~= 'string' or #options.label == 0 or #options.label > 100
        or options.label:find('%c') or not S.finite(options.width, 8, 4096)
        or not S.finite(options.height, 8, 4096) then return nil end
    if options.persist ~= nil and type(options.persist) ~= 'boolean' then return nil end
    if options.minVisiblePixels ~= nil and not S.finite(options.minVisiblePixels, 0, 4096) then return nil end
    if options.minVisibleFraction ~= nil and not S.finite(options.minVisibleFraction, 0, 1) then return nil end
    local minScale, maxScale = options.minScale or 0.5, options.maxScale or 2
    if not S.finite(minScale, 0.1, 4) or not S.finite(maxScale, minScale, 4) then return nil end
    local component = { key = owner .. ':' .. id, owner = owner, id = id, label = options.label,
        width = options.width, height = options.height, minScale = minScale, maxScale = maxScale,
        canHide = options.canHide ~= false, canScale = options.canScale ~= false,
        persist = options.persist ~= false,
        minVisiblePixels = options.minVisiblePixels, minVisibleFraction = options.minVisibleFraction }
    component.defaults = type(options.defaults) == 'table' and options.defaults or
        { x = 0.02, y = 0.02, scale = 1, visible = true, anchor = 'top-left' }
    component.defaults = S.layout(component.defaults, component)
    if not component.defaults then return nil end
    -- `defaults` is the factory placement -- the thing Reset goes back to -- and
    -- `layout` is where the widget is right now. They are only the same object for
    -- a consumer that has nowhere else to keep its placement. A consumer that owns
    -- its own storage (persist = false) used to have to pass its saved position as
    -- `defaults`, which made Reset restore the broken position it was being asked
    -- to escape from. Passing both separates "where it is" from "where it belongs".
    component.initial = type(options.layout) == 'table' and S.layout(options.layout, component) or nil
    return component
end
return S

local os_time = os.time
local lastTriggerTime = {}

--- Start a cooldown for a specific identifier and key.
--- ```lua
--- local citizenId = LT.Framework.GetPlayerCitizenId(source)
--- LT.Cooldown.Start(citizenId, 'gather', 5000) -- 5 seconds
--- ```
--- @param identifier string|number Cooldown identifier (like player citizenid)
--- @param key string Cooldown identifier
--- @param duration number Cooldown duration in milliseconds
--- @ltbridge export: Start
function StartCooldown(identifier, key, duration)
    if not identifier or not key then return end
    local identifierSrc = tostring(identifier)
    if not lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc] then lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc] = {} end

    local durationInSeconds = duration / 1000
    lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] = os_time() + durationInSeconds
end

--- Check if a specific cooldown is active.
--- ```lua
--- local citizenId = LT.Framework.GetPlayerCitizenId(source)
--- if LT.Cooldown.Check(citizenId, 'gather') then return end
--- ```
--- @param identifier string|number Cooldown identifier (like player citizenid)
--- @param key string Cooldown identifier
--- @return boolean
--- @ltbridge export: Check
function CheckCooldown(identifier, key)
    if not identifier or not key then return false end
    local identifierSrc = tostring(identifier)

    if not lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc] or not lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] then
        return false
    end

    if os_time() < lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] then
        return true
    end

    -- Cleanup expired
    lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] = nil
    return false
end

--- Get remaining cooldown time in milliseconds.
--- @param identifier string|number Cooldown identifier (like player citizenid)
--- @param key string Cooldown identifier
--- @return number remainingMs
--- @ltbridge export: Remaining
function GetCooldownRemaining(identifier, key)
    if not identifier or not key then return 0 end
    local identifierSrc = tostring(identifier)

    if not lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc] or not lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] then
        return 0
    end

    local remaining = lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] - os_time()
    if remaining > 0 then
        return math.floor(remaining * 1000)
    end

    lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] = nil
    return 0
end

--- Clear a specific cooldown early.
--- @param identifier string|number Cooldown identifier (like player citizenid)
--- @param key string Cooldown identifier
--- @ltbridge export: Clear
function ClearCooldown(identifier, key)
    if not identifier or not key then return end
    local identifierSrc = tostring(identifier)
    if lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc] then
        lastTriggerTime[identifierSrc][key] = nil
    end
end

--- Cleanup expired cooldowns to prevent memory leaks.
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        if next(lastTriggerTime) then
            for identifier, data in pairs(lastTriggerTime) do
                for key, time in pairs(data) do
                    if os_time() > time then
                        lastTriggerTime[identifier][key] = nil
                    end
                end
            end
        else
            Wait(120000) -- 2 minutes
        end
        Wait(60000)      -- 1 minute
    end
end)

function lib.closestVehicle(source, entity, radialSpace)
  assert(type(entity) == 'number', ('entity must be a number, received (%s)'):format(radialSpace))
  assert(type(radialSpace) == 'number', ('radialSpace must be a number, received (%s)'):format(radialSpace))
  assert(type(source) == 'number', ('source must be a number, received (%s)'):format(source))

  local coords<const> = GetEntityCoords(entity)
  local vehicles<const> = GetGamePool('CVehicle')

  local closestVehicle = nil
  local closestDistance = radialSpace

  for i = 1, #vehicles do
    local vehicle<const> = vehicles[i]
    local vehCoords<const> = GetEntityCoords(vehicle)
    local distance<const> = #(coords - vehCoords)

    if distance < closestDistance then
      closestDistance = distance
      closestVehicle = vehicle
    end
  end

  return closestVehicle
end
