-- Client-side action dispatch and the effect scheduler.
--
-- The server approves a row by answering with an owner and a handler name.
-- Handlers live in a table per owner, so a resource can only ever reach a handler
-- it registered itself — which is what makes dispatch safe to offer to every
-- resource rather than to one privileged plugin.
--
-- An effect is a handler that keeps running after the row is activated (infinite
-- ammo, god mode, a speed limiter). Because they outlive the menu they have to be
-- re-checked against permissions, stopped when a grant is revoked, and cleaned up
-- when the owning resource stops.

MenuActions = {}
local M = MenuActions
local S = MenuSchema

local dispatchers = {}

-- One thread serves every owner's effects, keyed by owner and name — a scheduler
-- per resource would be N threads waking on the same tick to do the same work.
-- The generation counter is how a faster effect replaces a sleeping scheduler: the
-- old generation notices it is stale on wake and exits rather than dying mid-tick.
local effects = {}
local running, schedulerGeneration, wakeAt = false, 0, 0

local function anyEffects()
    return next(effects) ~= nil
end

local function effectKey(owner, name)
    return owner .. '\0' .. name
end

local function startScheduler()
    schedulerGeneration = schedulerGeneration + 1
    local generation = schedulerGeneration
    running = true
    Platform.createThread(function()
        local last = Platform.now()
        while anyEffects() and generation == schedulerGeneration do
            local now, delay = Platform.now(), 1000
            -- A failing effect stops only itself: clearing the key `pairs` is
            -- currently visiting is the one mutation Lua permits mid-traversal.
            for key, effect in pairs(effects) do
                -- `now < last` is a timer wrap — everything is due.
                if now < last or now >= effect.due then
                    effect.due = now + effect.interval
                    local ok, err = pcall(effect.tick)
                    if not ok then
                        M.log(('effect %s stopped: %s'):format(key, tostring(err)))
                        local dispatcher = dispatchers[effect.owner]
                        if dispatcher then dispatcher:setEffect(effect.name, false) end
                    end
                end
                if effects[key] then delay = math.min(delay, math.max(0, effect.due - now)) end
            end
            last = now
            if anyEffects() and generation == schedulerGeneration then
                wakeAt = now + math.max(1, delay)
                Platform.wait(delay)
            end
        end
        if generation == schedulerGeneration then running, wakeAt = false, 0 end
    end)
end

function M.log(message)
    print('[tLib/menu] ' .. tostring(message))
end

-- An effect may be owned by an action or a list rather than a checkbox, and
-- publishing a boolean onto a list would overwrite the selected option.
local resolveItem = function() return nil end
function M.setItemResolver(fn)
    if type(fn) == 'function' then resolveItem = fn end
end

local D = {}
D.__index = D

--- Get (or create) the dispatcher for one resource. Handlers, stored state and
--- registered effects are all scoped to it.
function M.forOwner(owner)
    assert(type(owner) == 'string' and owner ~= '', 'an action dispatcher needs an owner')
    local existing = dispatchers[owner]
    if existing then return existing end
    local dispatcher = setmetatable({
        owner = owner,
        prefix = owner .. ':',
        handlers = {},
        states = {},
        cleanups = {},
        persisters = {},
        publisher = nil,
        effectsChanged = nil,
    }, D)
    dispatchers[owner] = dispatcher
    return dispatcher
end

function M.get(owner)
    return dispatchers[owner]
end

--- Every registered dispatcher, keyed by owner. The presentation pipeline walks
--- these to replay locally-held state onto a fresh snapshot.
function M.dispatchers()
    return dispatchers
end

--- Dispatch an approved action. The owner is supplied by the server's reply, so a
--- resource cannot reach another resource's handlers by naming them.
function M.execute(owner, name, value, context)
    local dispatcher = dispatchers[owner]
    if not dispatcher then return false, 'Unknown action owner' end
    return dispatcher:execute(name, value, context)
end

function D:register(name, handler)
    assert(type(name) == 'string' and S.callable(handler) and not self.handlers[name],
        'Duplicate or invalid action: ' .. tostring(name))
    self.handlers[name] = handler
end

function D:has(name)
    return self.handlers[name] ~= nil
end

function D:onCleanup(handler) self.cleanups[#self.cleanups + 1] = handler end

-- Persisters run after the handler returns successfully, so a rejected value is
-- never written. They hang off execute rather than publish because publish also
-- fires for permission revocation and for effects the engine stops itself — a
-- stored preference must not be overwritten by a row the server took away.
function D:onPersist(handler) self.persisters[#self.persisters + 1] = handler end
function D:bindPublisher(handler) self.publisher = handler end
function D:onEffectsChanged(handler) self.effectsChanged = handler end

function D:state(name, value)
    if value ~= nil then
        self.states[name] = self.states[name] or {}
        self.states[name].value = value
    end
    return self.states[name] and self.states[name].value
end

function D:publish(name, changes)
    local clean, err = S.patch(changes)
    assert(clean, err)
    self.states[name] = self.states[name] or {}
    for key, value in pairs(clean) do self.states[name][key] = value end
    if self.publisher then self.publisher(name, clean) end
end

--- Replay locally-held state onto a freshly received snapshot, for this owner's
--- rows only. A row belonging to another resource is left exactly as it arrived.
function D:decorate(value)
    for _, menu in ipairs(value.menus) do
        for _, item in ipairs(menu.items) do
            if item.id:sub(1, #self.prefix) == self.prefix then
                local saved = self.states[item.id:sub(#self.prefix + 1)]
                for key, current in pairs(saved or {}) do
                    if key ~= 'value' or S.value(item, current) then item[key] = current end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

function D:effectNames()
    local names = {}
    for _, effect in pairs(effects) do
        if effect.owner == self.owner then names[#names + 1] = effect.name end
    end
    return names
end

function D:hasEffects()
    return #self:effectNames() > 0
end

--- Stop any effect the player is no longer allowed to run. `allowed` is the
--- server's answer; anything not explicitly true is treated as revoked, so a
--- malformed or missing answer fails closed.
function D:applyPermissions(allowed, requested)
    for _, name in ipairs(requested or self:effectNames()) do
        if type(allowed) ~= 'table' or allowed[name] ~= true then self:setEffect(name, false) end
    end
end

--- Stop any effect whose row has vanished from the snapshot — the ACE was
--- revoked, or the owner hid the row.
function D:syncPermissions(value)
    local available = {}
    for _, menu in ipairs(value.menus) do
        for _, item in ipairs(menu.items) do
            if not item.disabled and item.id:sub(1, #self.prefix) == self.prefix then
                available[item.id:sub(#self.prefix + 1)] = true
            end
        end
    end
    for _, name in ipairs(self:effectNames()) do
        if not available[name] then self:setEffect(name, false) end
    end
end

function D:setEffect(name, enabled, definition)
    local key = effectKey(self.owner, name)
    local previous = effects[key]
    if previous then
        effects[key] = nil
        if previous.stop then
            local ok, err = pcall(previous.stop)
            if not ok then M.log('effect cleanup failed: ' .. tostring(err)) end
        end
    end
    if enabled then
        assert(type(definition) == 'table' and S.callable(definition.tick), 'Invalid effect definition')
        local interval = math.max(0, tonumber(definition.interval) or 0)
        local effect = { owner = self.owner, name = name, tick = definition.tick, stop = definition.stop,
            interval = interval, due = Platform.now() + math.max(1, interval) }
        effects[key] = effect
        -- Ticked once now rather than on the next scheduler pass; a first tick
        -- that throws un-registers rather than leaving a broken effect scheduled.
        local ok, err = pcall(effect.tick)
        if not ok then
            self:setEffect(name, false)
            error(err, 0)
        end
    end
    local item = resolveItem(self.owner, name)
    if not item or item.kind == 'toggle' then self:publish(name, { value = effects[key] ~= nil }) end
    if self.effectsChanged then self.effectsChanged(self:hasEffects()) end
    if not effects[key] then return end
    if running and wakeAt <= effects[key].due then return end
    startScheduler()
end

function D:stopEffects()
    for _, name in ipairs(self:effectNames()) do self:setEffect(name, false) end
end

function D:execute(name, value, context)
    local handler = self.handlers[name]
    if not handler then return false, 'Unknown approved action' end
    local ok, err = pcall(handler, value, context)
    if not ok then return false, tostring(err):sub(1, 256) end
    -- Autosave never fails the change the player just made.
    for index = 1, #self.persisters do
        local saved, reason = pcall(self.persisters[index], name)
        if not saved then M.log(('autosave failed for %s: %s'):format(name, tostring(reason))) end
    end
    return true
end

function D:cleanup()
    self:stopEffects()
    for index = #self.cleanups, 1, -1 do
        local ok, err = pcall(self.cleanups[index])
        if not ok then M.log('module cleanup failed: ' .. tostring(err)) end
    end
end

--- Tear down a resource's dispatcher when it stops, so its effects stop ticking
--- against handlers that are gone.
function M.dropOwner(owner)
    local dispatcher = dispatchers[owner]
    if not dispatcher then return false end
    dispatcher:cleanup()
    dispatchers[owner] = nil
    return true
end

function M.cleanupAll()
    for owner in pairs(dispatchers) do M.dropOwner(owner) end
end

function M.anyEffects()
    return anyEffects()
end

return MenuActions

local string_format = string.format
local tonumber = tonumber

local debugTypes <const> = {
    ['success'] = { mode = 3, color = 2 },
    ['error'] = { mode = 1, color = 1 },
    ['warning'] = { mode = 2, color = 3 },
    ['info'] = { mode = 3, color = 4 },
    ['verbose'] = { mode = 4, color = 5 },
}

local function handleException(result, value)
    if type(value) == 'function' then
        return tostring(value)
    end
    return result
end

--- Format the data to a string.
--- @param ... any Data to format.
--- @return string Formatted data.
local function format(message, ...)
    local data = { ... }

    for i = 1, #data do
        local v = data[i]

        if type(v) == "table" then
            data[i] = json.encode(v, {
                indent = true,
                exception = handleException
            })
        elseif type(v) == "boolean" then
            data[i] = v and "true" or "false"
        elseif type(v) ~= "string" then
            data[i] = tostring(v)
        end
    end

    return string_format(message, table.unpack(data))
end

--- Set debug mode.
---
--- **0**: `Disabled` (Not Recommended)
---
--- **1**: `Errors` (Default)
---
--- **2**: `Errors + Warnings`
---
--- **3**: `Except Verbose`
---
--- **4**: `All Messages`
---
--- @param mode? number
--- @ltbridge export: SetMode
function SetDebugMode(mode)

end

--- Prints a formatted and detailed (with file and line info) debug message.
--- @param message string Message to print.
--- @param type? 'info'|'success'|'error'|'warning'|'verbose'
--- @param ...? any Format parameters.
--- @ltbridge export: Detailed
function DebugDetailed(message, type, ...)
    if not type then type = 'verbose' end
    local data = debugTypes[type]
    if not data then return end
    if tonumber(debugMode) < tonumber(data.mode) then return end

    local info = debug.getinfo(2, 'Sl')
    local source = info and info.short_src or 'unknown'
    local line = info and info.currentline or -1

    print(string_format('^%d[%s] %s:%d: ^7%s^7', data.color, type:upper(), source, line, format(message, ...)))

--- Prints a formatted debug message.

function DebugPrint(message, type, ...)
    if not type then type = 'verbose' end
    local data = debugTypes[type]
    if not data then return end
    if tonumber(debugMode) < tonumber(data.mode) then return end

    print(string_format('^%d[%s]^7 %s^7', data.color, type:upper(), format(message, ...)))

--
-- A snapshot says what a player is allowed to do; it cannot say what they can do
-- right now -- the mod slots of the car they are sitting in, the tints a weapon
-- supports, whether anyone is close enough to target. That is local, changes
-- second to second, and belongs to whichever resource owns the rows.
--
-- So this file is pipeline only: it decides which pages to build, hands them to
-- the registered presenters, gives them the two operations they all need (narrow
-- a list, disable a row with a reason) plus a cache that empties itself when the
-- world moves, and assembles each page's contextKey from what they contribute.
--
-- The narrowed copy must never be fed back into permission or effect
-- reconciliation: those run against the raw snapshot, and a row disabled here
-- because the player got out of the car is not a revoked grant.
--
-- `authority`, present()'s second argument, is scoped to the pass — the most
-- expensive decision in the menu. A cross-resource presenter crosses an export
-- boundary that serialises every argument, so passing the whole hydrated
-- snapshot msgpacked the entire catalogue once per presenter per pass. Against
-- tMenu's catalogue (215 pages, ~51,000 option labels, 3.4 MB encoded), timed
-- with GetNetworkTimeAccurate since GetGameTimer does not advance within a
-- frame: 43-99 ms with the whole snapshot as `raw`, 0-1 ms with it emptied —
-- the payload was the whole cost.

if _TLIB_SIDE ~= 'client' then return end

MenuContext = {}
local C = MenuContext
local S = MenuSchema

local presenters = {}

-- Presenters ask the game the same questions repeatedly within a pass.
local cache, cacheKey, cacheSize = {}, nil, 0

function C.invalidate()
    cache, cacheKey, cacheSize = {}, nil, 0
    for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
        if presenter.invalidate then pcall(presenter.invalidate) end
    end
end

--- Memoize one question about the current world. The 512 cap is a ceiling, not
--- an LRU: at 512 the whole cache is dropped rather than evicted entry by entry.
function C.cached(key, fn)
    if cache[key] == nil then
        local result = fn() -- an exception never reaches the cache
        if cacheSize >= 512 then cache, cacheSize = {}, 0 end
        cache[key], cacheSize = result, cacheSize + 1
    end
    return cache[key]
end


--- Take a row out of play and say why -- a greyed row with no explanation reads
--- as a bug.
function C.disable(row, reason)
    row.disabled, row.description = true, reason
end

--- Keep only the options a predicate accepts.
function C.narrow(row, predicate, reason)
    local options = setmetatable({}, { __jsontype = 'array' })
    local selected = false
    for _, option in ipairs(row.options or {}) do
        if predicate(option.value) then
            options[#options + 1] = option
            if option.value == row.value then selected = true end
        end
    end
    row.options = options
    if not selected then row.value = nil end
    if #options == 0 then C.disable(row, reason) end
end

local function equal(a, b)
    if type(a) ~= type(b) then return false end
    if type(a) ~= 'table' then return a == b end
    for k, v in pairs(a) do if not equal(v, b[k]) then return false end end
    for k in pairs(b) do if a[k] == nil then return false end end
    return true
end
C.equal = equal


--- Register one resource's presentation logic. Every field is optional -- a
--- resource that only wants its own stored state on its rows registers nothing,
--- because MenuActions already does that.
function C.register(owner, presenter)
    if type(owner) ~= 'string' or owner == '' then return false, 'A presenter needs an owner' end
    if type(presenter) ~= 'table' then return false, 'A presenter must be a table' end
    for _, field in ipairs({ 'expand', 'identity', 'present', 'contextKey', 'invalidate' }) do
        if presenter[field] ~= nil and not S.callable(presenter[field]) then
            return false, 'presenter.' .. field .. ' must be a function'
        end
    end
    for index, existing in ipairs(presenters) do
        if existing.owner == owner then
            presenters[index] = { owner = owner, expand = presenter.expand, identity = presenter.identity,
                present = presenter.present, contextKey = presenter.contextKey, invalidate = presenter.invalidate }
            C.invalidate()
            return true
        end
    end
    presenters[#presenters + 1] = { owner = owner, expand = presenter.expand, identity = presenter.identity,
        present = presenter.present, contextKey = presenter.contextKey, invalidate = presenter.invalidate }
    C.invalidate()
    return true
end

function C.unregister(owner)
    for index, existing in ipairs(presenters) do
        if existing.owner == owner then
            table.remove(presenters, index)
            C.invalidate()
            return true
        end
    end
    return false
end

function C.count() return #presenters end

local function guard(stage, owner, fn, ...)
    local ok, result = pcall(fn, ...)
    if ok then return result end
    print(('[tLib/menu] %s presenter %s failed: %s'):format(owner, stage, tostring(result)))
    return nil
end

--- Build the presentable form of `requested`, or of every page when it is nil.
--- `raw` is the hydrated, permission-filtered snapshot.
function C.present(raw, requested)
    local wanted
    if requested then
        wanted = {}
        local function want(id) if type(id) == 'string' then wanted[id] = true end end
        for _, id in ipairs(requested) do want(id) end
        local queue = {}
        for id in pairs(wanted) do queue[#queue + 1] = id end
        for _, id in ipairs(queue) do
            for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
                if presenter.expand then guard('expand', presenter.owner, presenter.expand, id, want) end
            end
        end
    end

    local value = { version = raw.version, visible = raw.visible, capabilities = raw.capabilities, menus = {} }
    for _, menu in ipairs(raw.menus) do
        if not wanted or wanted[menu.id] then value.menus[#value.menus + 1] = S.copy(menu) end
    end

    local authority = { version = raw.version, visible = raw.visible, capabilities = raw.capabilities,
        menus = {}, ids = setmetatable({}, { __jsontype = 'array' }) }
    local rawById = {}
    for _, menu in ipairs(raw.menus) do
        rawById[menu.id] = menu
        authority.ids[#authority.ids + 1] = menu.id
        if not wanted or wanted[menu.id] then authority.menus[#authority.menus + 1] = menu end
    end
    setmetatable(authority.menus, { __jsontype = 'array' })
    function authority.page(id) return rawById[id] end

    local parts = {}
    for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
        if presenter.identity then
            parts[#parts + 1] = presenter.owner .. '=' .. tostring(guard('identity', presenter.owner, presenter.identity))
        end
    end
    local key = table.concat(parts, '|')
    if key ~= cacheKey then
        cache, cacheKey, cacheSize = {}, key, 0
        -- A presenter in another VM cannot see this wipe, so it has to be told.
        for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
            if presenter.invalidate then guard('invalidate', presenter.owner, presenter.invalidate) end
        end
    end

    for _, dispatcher in pairs(MenuActions.dispatchers()) do dispatcher:decorate(value) end
    for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
        if presenter.present then
            local result = guard('present', presenter.owner, presenter.present, value, authority)
            if type(result) == 'table' and type(result.menus) == 'table' then value = result end
        end
    end

    for _, menu in ipairs(value.menus) do
        setmetatable(menu.items, { __jsontype = 'array' })
        for _, row in ipairs(menu.items) do
            if row.options then setmetatable(row.options, { __jsontype = 'array' }) end
        end
    end
    setmetatable(value.menus, { __jsontype = 'array' })

    for _, menu in ipairs(value.menus) do
        local identities = {}
        for _, presenter in ipairs(presenters) do
            if presenter.contextKey then
                local part = guard('contextKey', presenter.owner, presenter.contextKey, menu)
                if type(part) == 'string' and part ~= '' then identities[#identities + 1] = part end
            end
        end
        if #identities > 0 then
            if menu.contextKey then table.insert(identities, 1, menu.contextKey) end
            local assembled = table.concat(identities, '|')
            menu.contextKey = #assembled <= 192 and assembled or MenuCatalog.fingerprint(identities)
        end
    end
    return value
end

return MenuContext

--- Send dispatch alert to given jobs.

-- Keyboard and gamepad navigation for the open menu, plus the input suppression
-- that stops navigating a menu from also driving the character.
--
-- Built out of GTA V control IDs, so the whole loop is FiveM-only and every entry
-- point degrades to a no-op elsewhere. It emits protocol-free names -- 'navigate',
-- 'input', 'hidden' -- through a sender the menu client installs, so no NUI wire
-- string appears here.

MenuInput = {}
local I = MenuInput

local visible, typing, generation = false, false, 0
local modal, suppressUntilRelease = false, false
local emit = function() end

--- Installed by the menu client, so the NUI protocol can be renamed without
--- touching a control ID.
function I.bindSender(fn)
    if type(fn) == 'function' then emit = fn end
end

function I.setModal(active)
    modal = active == true
    if not modal then suppressUntilRelease = true end
end

-- Accept and back fire on release: a submenu opening under a still-held Enter
-- must not immediately activate its own first row.
local bindings = {
    { name = 'back', controls = { 177, 202 }, release = true },
    { name = 'accept', controls = { 176, 201, 106 }, release = true },
    -- 181/180 are the scroll wheel: single-frame presses, so they never feed the
    -- hold ladder, and they yield to the weapon wheel below.
    { name = 'up', controls = { 172, 188 }, wheel = { 181 }, repeatable = true },
    { name = 'down', controls = { 173, 187 }, wheel = { 180 }, repeatable = true },
    { name = 'left', controls = { 174, 189 }, repeatable = true },
    { name = 'right', controls = { 175, 190 }, repeatable = true },
}
-- 44/21/22/23/75 share a physical controller button with accept/back; letting
-- them through makes the character jump or leave a vehicle while navigating.
local blocked = { 20, 24, 25, 27, 44, 68, 69, 70, 92, 114, 140, 141, 142, 200, 257, 263, 264 }
-- Only while the player is in a vehicle.
local blockedInVehicle = { 73, 74, 80, 81, 82, 85, 99, 100, 332, 333, 357 }

-- First repeat after 200ms, then accelerating with the run length. A long vehicle
-- or weapon list is unusable at a flat rate.
local function repeatDelay(times)
    if times > 60 then return 25 elseif times > 25 then return 50
    elseif times > 5 then return 100 elseif times > 2 then return 150 end
    return 200
end

local function yes(value) return value == true or value == 1 end

-- The weapon wheel is disabled only for a gamepad sitting on a slider or list row,
-- where left/right would fight it; the browser reports the highlighted row kind.
local valueRow = false
function I.setValueRow(active) valueRow = active == true end

-- Suspension, not closure. A real close resets the browser to the main page and
-- drops every uncommitted selector and slider draft, so the pause menu or a screen
-- fade would throw away a half-dialed row. Suspending stops forwarding and
-- blocking native input and asks the browser to stand down, leaving the session,
-- page and drafts intact.
--
-- Death is not one of these: the state it was configuring no longer exists.
local suspended = false
local function suspend(active)
    if suspended == active then return end
    suspended = active
    -- Text entry holds NUI keyboard focus and the pause menu cannot be used through
    -- it. Conditional because this runs on a frame boundary -- an unconditional
    -- I.text(false) would post a message on every suspension.
    if active and typing then I.text(false) end
    emit('hidden', active)
end
function I.text(active)
    if active and (not visible or modal or (not typing and _TLIB_IS_FIVEM
        and type(IsNuiFocused) == 'function' and yes(IsNuiFocused()))) then return false end
    if typing and not active then suppressUntilRelease = true end
    local hadFocus = typing
    typing = active == true
    if _TLIB_IS_FIVEM and (typing or hadFocus) then
        SetNuiFocus(typing, false)
        SetNuiFocusKeepInput(false)
    end
    emit('input', typing)
    return true
end
function I.isTyping() return typing end

function I.setVisible(active, onClose)
    generation = generation + 1
    visible = active == true
    I.text(false)
    -- Closing while suspended must not leave the browser hidden, or the next open
    -- draws nothing.
    suspend(false)
    if not visible or not _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then return end
    local current, repeats = generation, {}
    Platform.createThread(function()
        while visible and current == generation do
            if yes(IsEntityDead(PlayerPedId())) then onClose(); break end
            -- A fade means the game is showing the player something else, and no
            -- fade covers the browser's panel. Probed rather than called outright,
            -- like every other optional native here.
            local faded = type(IsScreenFadedOut) == 'function' and yes(IsScreenFadedOut())
            suspend(yes(IsPauseMenuActive()) or faded)
            -- Dialogs and other resources' NUI own their keyboard while focused;
            -- their closing key release is not a menu action.
            local nuiFocused = type(IsNuiFocused) == 'function' and yes(IsNuiFocused())
            if nuiFocused then suppressUntilRelease = true end
            if not suspended and not typing and not modal and not nuiFocused then
                local ped = PlayerPedId()
                local inVehicle = yes(IsPedInAnyVehicle(ped, false))
                local gamepad = not yes(IsInputDisabled(2))
                -- Holding the weapon-select key hands the wheel back to weapon
                -- switching and the menu ignores it.
                local weaponWheel = yes(IsControlPressed(0, 37)) or yes(IsDisabledControlPressed(0, 37))
                for _, control in ipairs(blocked) do DisableControlAction(0, control, true) end
                if inVehicle then
                    for _, control in ipairs(blockedInVehicle) do DisableControlAction(0, control, true) end
                end
                if not weaponWheel then
                    DisableControlAction(0, 16, true); DisableControlAction(0, 17, true)
                end
                if gamepad and valueRow then DisableControlAction(0, 37, true) end
                for _, binding in ipairs(bindings) do
                    for _, control in ipairs(binding.controls) do DisableControlAction(0, control, true) end
                    if binding.wheel and not weaponWheel then
                        for _, control in ipairs(binding.wheel) do DisableControlAction(0, control, true) end
                    end
                end
                -- Controller accept/back must not also jump, sprint or enter a vehicle.
                if gamepad then
                    for _, control in ipairs({ 21, 22, 23, 75 }) do DisableControlAction(0, control, true) end
                end
                -- Suppression lifts on the same frame the held key is released, and
                -- accept/back fire on that edge. Skip the frame or dismissing a
                -- prompt immediately re-activates a row.
                local justLifted = false
                if suppressUntilRelease then
                    local held = false
                    for _, binding in ipairs(bindings) do
                        for _, control in ipairs(binding.controls) do held = held or yes(IsDisabledControlPressed(0, control)) end
                    end
                    if not held then suppressUntilRelease = false; repeats = {}; justLifted = true end
                end
                local now = Platform.now()
                for _, binding in ipairs(bindings) do
                    if suppressUntilRelease or justLifted then break end
                    local pressed, held = false, false
                    for _, control in ipairs(binding.controls) do
                        if binding.release then pressed = pressed or yes(IsDisabledControlJustReleased(0, control))
                        else pressed = pressed or yes(IsDisabledControlJustPressed(0, control)) end
                        held = held or yes(IsDisabledControlPressed(0, control))
                    end
                    -- A wheel notch is a one-frame press with no hold: it moves the
                    -- row once and never enters the ladder below.
                    if binding.wheel and not weaponWheel then
                        for _, control in ipairs(binding.wheel) do
                            pressed = pressed or yes(IsDisabledControlJustPressed(0, control))
                        end
                    end
                    local state = repeats[binding.name]
                    local fire = pressed
                    if pressed then repeats[binding.name] = { due = now + 200, times = 0 }
                    elseif binding.repeatable and held then
                        if state and now >= state.due then
                            fire = true
                            state.times = state.times + 1
                            state.due = now + repeatDelay(state.times)
                        elseif not state then repeats[binding.name] = { due = now + 200, times = 0 } end
                    elseif not held then repeats[binding.name] = nil end
                    if fire then emit('navigate', binding.name); break end
                end
            end
            Platform.wait(0)
        end
    end)
end

--- Bind the search key. The command name comes from whoever configures the
--- interface, since it sits alongside that resource's own open command in the
--- player's keybind list.
function I.bindSearchKey(command, key, label)
    if not _TLIB_IS_FIVEM or type(command) ~= 'string' or command == '' then return false end
    RegisterCommand(command, function()
        if visible then I.text(not typing) end
    end, false)
    RegisterKeyMapping(command, label or 'Search the open menu', 'keyboard', key or 'F3')
    return true
end

function I.cleanup() I.setVisible(false) end

return MenuInput

-- Asking the player to type something without handing the browser the keyboard.
-- The menu draws and the game keeps the input; NUI focus for a text field would
-- put a mouse cursor over a controller-navigated menu and swallow movement keys
-- while the field was open. GTA's onscreen keyboard -- what the pause menu uses --
-- avoids both. One prompt for the whole interface, since there is one screen.

if _TLIB_SIDE ~= 'client' then return end

MenuPrompt = {}
local P = MenuPrompt

-- Registered at call time with the caller's title. Arbitrary but global to the
-- game session, hence the prefix.
local TEXT_ENTRY = 'TLIB_MENU_INPUT'

local prompting = false

--- Always safe to call: cancels whatever is open and returns the menu to ordinary
--- navigation. The client engine calls it on close and on shutdown.
function P.release()
    if prompting and type(CancelOnscreenKeyboard) == 'function' then pcall(CancelOnscreenKeyboard) end
    prompting = false
    if MenuInput then MenuInput.setModal(false) end
end

function P.active() return prompting end

--- Ask for a line of text. Blocks the calling thread until the player commits or
--- cancels, so call it from an action handler and never from the presentation path.
---
--- Returns the string on commit and nil on cancel. Everything else -- a second
--- concurrent prompt, an action cancelled underneath it, a timeout -- is raised
--- with error(message, 0), the shape the dispatcher reports to the player rather
--- than logging as a crash.
function P.text(title, initial, maximum, context)
    assert(MenuSchema.text(title, 128), 'Invalid input title')
    assert(type(maximum) == 'number' and maximum % 1 == 0 and maximum >= 1 and maximum <= 128, 'Invalid input length')
    assert(type(initial) == 'string' and #initial <= maximum and not initial:find('%c'), 'Invalid initial input')
    if not _TLIB_IS_FIVEM then error('Text input is unavailable on this platform', 0) end
    if prompting then error('Another input is already active', 0) end
    local function active() return context and context.isActive and context.isActive() end
    if not active() then error('Action cancelled', 0) end
    local ok, result = pcall(function()
        prompting = true
        if MenuInput then MenuInput.text(false); MenuInput.setModal(true) end
        AddTextEntry(TEXT_ENTRY, title)
        DisplayOnscreenKeyboard(1, TEXT_ENTRY, '', initial, '', '', '', maximum)
        -- Two deadlines: the wall clock catches a player who walked away, the
        -- frame count catches a paused or hitching game, where the wall clock
        -- would expire without the keyboard ever being polled.
        local started, frames = Platform.now(), 0
        while prompting and active() do
            local state = UpdateOnscreenKeyboard()
            if state == 1 then
                local value = GetOnscreenKeyboardResult()
                if type(value) ~= 'string' or #value > maximum or value:find('%c') then error('Invalid input text', 0) end
                return value
            end
            if state == 2 or state == 3 then return nil end
            frames = frames + 1
            if Platform.now() - started >= 60000 or frames >= 36000 then error('Text input timed out', 0) end
            Platform.wait(0)
        end
        error('Action cancelled', 0)
    end)
    P.release()
    if not ok then error(result, 0) end
    -- The action may have been cancelled while the player typed; committing into a
    -- dead action is worse than losing the text.
    if not active() then error('Action cancelled', 0) end
    return result
end

return MenuPrompt

local isServer <const> = IsDuplicityVersion()

--- Triggers network event with formatted name.
---
--- `Client` -> `Server`
---
--- `Server` -> `Client`
---
--- **Lua Example:**
--- ```lua
--- local emitNet = LT.Events.EmitNet
---
--- -- Client example:
--- emitNet('exampleEvent', 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- -- Turns into:
--- TriggerServerEvent('resourcename:server:exampleEvent', 'arg1', 'arg2')
---
--- -- Server example with one target:
--- emitNet('exampleEvent', source, 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- -- Turns into:
--- TriggerClientEvent('resourcename:client:exampleEvent', source, 'arg1', 'arg2')
---
--- -- Server example with multiple targets:
--- emitNet('exampleEvent', { 1, 2, 3 }, 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- -- Turns into:
--- TriggerClientEvent('resourcename:client:exampleEvent', 1, 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- TriggerClientEvent('resourcename:client:exampleEvent', 2, 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- TriggerClientEvent('resourcename:client:exampleEvent', 3, 'arg1', 'arg2')
--- ```
--- @param name string Event name
--- @param ...? any Event arguments (Optional)
--- @ltbridge export: EmitNet
function EventEmitNet(name, ...)
    local eventName = GetEventName(name, true)
    if isServer then
        local target = ...

        ltassert(type(target) == 'table' or type(target) == 'number', 'EmitNet: invalid target type on event (%s) expected table or number, got %s',
            name, type(target))

-- Lua mirrors the theme registry, so it can validate and answer reads without a
-- UI round trip.

ThemeExports  = {}

local log     = Logger.create('tLib/theme')

local ui      = nil
local _themes = {}

local function assertUI(fname)
    if not ui then
        log(fname .. ': Theme subsystem not initialised (ui is nil)', 4)
        return false
    end
    return true
end

local function assertId(fname, id)
    if type(id) ~= 'string' or id == '' then
        log(fname .. ': id must be a non-empty string', 3)
        return false
    end
    return true
end

local function shallowCopy(t)
    if type(t) ~= 'table' then return t end
    local copy = {}
    for k, v in pairs(t) do copy[k] = v end
    return copy
end

function ThemeExports.register(webui)
    ui = webui

    local function registerExport(name, fn)
        Platform.export('tLib', name, fn)
    end

    -- Register a theme, or replace one with the same id.
    --
    --   opts.cssVars  name -> value, WITHOUT the leading "--":
    --                 { primary = "262 83% 58%", radius = "0.75rem" }
    --   opts.extends  id of a registered theme to inherit from; these cssVars
    --                 overlay its own
    --   opts.font     font-family, sets --font-sans
    --   opts.fontSize percentage, sets the html font-size
    registerExport('AddTheme', function(id, opts)
        if not assertUI('AddTheme') then return false end
        if not assertId('AddTheme', id) then return false end
        if type(opts) ~= 'table' then
            log('AddTheme: opts must be a table', 3)
            return false
        end

        local def = {
            id          = id,
            name        = type(opts.name) == 'string' and opts.name ~= '' and opts.name or id,
            description = type(opts.description) == 'string' and opts.description or nil,
            extends     = type(opts.extends) == 'string' and opts.extends ~= '' and opts.extends or nil,
            font        = type(opts.font) == 'string' and opts.font ~= '' and opts.font or nil,
            fontSize    = type(opts.fontSize) == 'string' and opts.fontSize ~= '' and opts.fontSize or nil,
        }

        -- cssVars must be a flat string -> string map.
        if type(opts.cssVars) == 'table' then
            local vars = {}
            for k, v in pairs(opts.cssVars) do
                if type(k) == 'string' and type(v) == 'string' then
                    vars[k] = v
                else
                    log('AddTheme: cssVars entry "' .. tostring(k) .. '" skipped (key and value must both be strings)', 3)
                end
            end
            def.cssVars = vars
        end

        _themes[id] = def
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'addTheme', def)

        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:theme:added', id)
        return true
    end)

    -- Removing the active theme clears the :root override; store.ts handles that.
    registerExport('RemoveTheme', function(id)
        if not assertUI('RemoveTheme') then return false end
        if not assertId('RemoveTheme', id) then return false end

        if not _themes[id] then
            log('RemoveTheme: theme "' .. id .. '" is not registered', 3)
            return false
        end

        _themes[id] = nil
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'removeTheme', { id = id })
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:theme:removed', id)
        return true
    end)

    -- Applies the theme's vars to :root, so every component without a theme of
    -- its own inherits them. An empty id reverts to the base vars in global.css.
    registerExport('SetTheme', function(id)
        if not assertUI('SetTheme') then return false end

        if id == '' then
            Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'setTheme', { id = '' })
            Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:theme:set', '')
            return true
        end

        if not assertId('SetTheme', id) then return false end

        if not _themes[id] then
            log('SetTheme: theme "' .. id .. '" is not registered — call AddTheme first', 3)
            return false
        end

        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'setTheme', { id = id })
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:theme:set', id)
        return true
    end)

    registerExport('GetThemes', function()
        local copy = {}
        for id, def in pairs(_themes) do
            copy[id] = shallowCopy(def)
            -- cssVars is nested; copy it too, or callers can mutate the registry.
            if type(def.cssVars) == 'table' then
                copy[id].cssVars = shallowCopy(def.cssVars)
            end
        end
        return copy
    end)

    registerExport('GetTheme', function(id)
        if not assertId('GetTheme', id) then return nil end
        local def = _themes[id]
        if not def then return nil end
        local copy = shallowCopy(def)
        if type(def.cssVars) == 'table' then
            copy.cssVars = shallowCopy(def.cssVars)
        end
        return copy
    end)
end

    else
        RegisterNetEvent(event)
    end
end

ToastExports = {}
local log = Logger.create('tLib/toast')
local ui, stopped = nil, false
local entries, idCounter = {}, 0
local durations = { success = 4000, error = 6000, warning = 5000, info = 4000, loading = 0 }
local MAX_PER_OWNER, MAX_TOTAL = 32, 256

local function caller()
    local owner = Platform.getInvokingResource()
    if type(owner) == 'string' and owner ~= '' then return owner end
    log('Toast export requires an invoking resource', 3)
end

local function wireId(owner, id)
    return tostring(#owner) .. ':' .. owner .. ':' .. id
end

local function validDuration(value)
    return type(value) == 'number' and value >= 0 and value <= 2147483647
end

-- The short spellings are mapped, not refused: `durations` above is the whole
-- type vocabulary, and `warn` is not in it. Three resources independently
-- passed it for the same notice anyway, each falling through to neutral
-- `info` where it meant amber `warning` — the fallback is correct for a
-- genuinely unknown type, nothing failed loudly.
--
-- `warn`/`warning` and `err`/`error` are the two pairs any Lua author reaches
-- for interchangeably (`warn` is a global in several runtimes, `err` the
-- idiomatic second-return name), so mapping them closes the class rather than
-- patching each instance.
--
-- The log stays for anything else: silently rendering an unknown type as info
-- is what hid these three for as long as it did.
local ALIASES = { warn = 'warning', err = 'error' }

local function resolveType(value)
    if type(value) ~= 'string' then
        log('Unknown toast type, defaulting to info', 3)
        return 'info'
    end
    if durations[value] ~= nil then return value end
    local aliased = ALIASES[value]
    if aliased and durations[aliased] ~= nil then return aliased end
    log('Unknown toast type, defaulting to info', 3)
    return 'info'
end

local function remove(key, notify)
    local entry = entries[key]
    if not entry then return false end
    entries[key] = nil
    if entry.timer then Platform.clearTimeout(entry.timer) end
    if notify and ui then Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'dismissToast', { id = key }) end
    return true
end

local function schedule(key, entry, duration)
    if entry.timer then Platform.clearTimeout(entry.timer) end
    entry.timer = nil
    -- Fence timers as well as entries: a type/duration update reuses the entry.
    entry.revision = entry.revision + 1
    local revision = entry.revision
    local delay = duration and duration > 0 and duration or durations[entry.type]
    if delay > 0 then
        entry.timer = Platform.setTimeout(function()
            if entries[key] == entry and entry.revision == revision then remove(key, true) end
        end, delay)
    end
end

local function owned(id)
    if stopped or not ui or type(id) ~= 'string' or id == '' then return end
    local owner = caller()
    if not owner then return end
    local key = wireId(owner, id)
    return entries[key], key
end

function ToastExports.register(webui)
    ui = webui

    -- IDs are local to the producer. Return values and public events keep that
    -- local ID; the renderer sees a namespaced ID so producers cannot collide.
    Platform.export('tLib', 'ShowToast', function(id, toastType, title, description, duration, theme)
        if stopped or not ui then return nil end
        local owner = caller()
        if not owner then return nil end
        if type(id) ~= 'string' or id == '' then
            repeat
                idCounter = idCounter + 1
                id = 'tlib_toast_' .. tostring(idCounter)
            until not entries[wireId(owner, id)]
        end
        local key = wireId(owner, id)
        if not entries[key] then
            local total, ownerCount = 0, 0
            for _, entry in pairs(entries) do
                total = total + 1
                if entry.owner == owner then ownerCount = ownerCount + 1 end
            end
            if total >= MAX_TOTAL or ownerCount >= MAX_PER_OWNER then
                return nil, 'Too many active toasts'
            end
        end
        remove(key, false)
        toastType = resolveType(toastType)
        local entry = { owner = owner, id = id, type = toastType, revision = 0 }
        entries[key] = entry
        duration = validDuration(duration) and duration or nil
        title = type(title) == 'string' and title or ''
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'showToast', {
            id = key, type = toastType, title = title,
            description = type(description) == 'string' and description or nil,
            duration = duration,
            theme = type(theme) == 'string' and theme ~= '' and theme or nil,
        })
        schedule(key, entry, duration)
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:toast:shown', id, toastType, title, owner)
        return id
    end)

    -- Text/theme-only patches retain their deadline. Type changes and explicit
    -- durations restart it; duration=0 restores the current type's default.
    Platform.export('tLib', 'UpdateToast', function(id, changes)
        local entry, key = owned(id)
        if not entry or type(changes) ~= 'table' then return false end
        local patch = {}
        if type(changes.type) == 'string' then patch.type = resolveType(changes.type) end
        if type(changes.title) == 'string' then patch.title = changes.title end
        if type(changes.description) == 'string' then patch.description = changes.description end
        if type(changes.theme) == 'string' then patch.theme = changes.theme end
        if validDuration(changes.duration) then patch.duration = changes.duration end
        if next(patch) == nil then return false end
        if patch.type then entry.type = patch.type end
        if patch.type or patch.duration ~= nil then schedule(key, entry, patch.duration) end
        Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'updateToast', { id = key, changes = patch })
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:toast:updated', id, patch, entry.owner)
        return true
    end)

    Platform.export('tLib', 'DismissToast', function(id)
        local entry, key = owned(id)
        if not entry then return false end
        remove(key, true)
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:toast:dismissed', id, entry.owner)
        return true
    end)

    -- Public bulk dismissal is producer-scoped, never a global UI reset.
    Platform.export('tLib', 'DismissAll', function()
        if stopped or not ui then return false end
        local owner = caller()
        if not owner then return false end
        for key, entry in pairs(entries) do
            if entry.owner == owner then remove(key, true) end
        end
        Platform.TriggerEvent('tLib:toast:dismissedAll', owner)
        return true
    end)
end

AddEventHandler('onClientResourceStop', function(owner)
    for key, entry in pairs(entries) do
        if entry.owner == owner then remove(key, true) end
    end
end)

Platform.onShutdown(function()
    stopped = true
    for key in pairs(entries) do remove(key, false) end
    if ui then Platform.sendUIEvent(ui, 'dismissAllToasts', {}) end
    ui = nil
end)

end

local function readField(xPlayer, key)
    if type(xPlayer.getMeta) == 'function' then
        local ok, value = pcall(xPlayer.getMeta, key)
        if ok and value ~= nil then return value end
    end
    if type(xPlayer.get) == 'function' then
        local ok, value = pcall(xPlayer.get, key)

    end

function Bridge.GetJob(src)
    local xPlayer = getPlayer(src)
    if not xPlayer or not xPlayer.job then return end
    local job = xPlayer.job
    return job.name, tonumber(job.grade) or 0, job.onDuty ~= false, job.label or job.name
end

function Bridge.GetCharName(src)
    local xPlayer = getPlayer(src)
    if not xPlayer then return Bridge.SplitName(GetPlayerName(src)) end
    local first, last = readField(xPlayer, 'firstName'), readField(xPlayer, 'lastName')
    if type(first) == 'string' and first ~= '' then
        return first, type(last) == 'string' and last or ''
    end
    return Bridge.SplitName(xPlayer.getName and xPlayer.getName() or GetPlayerName(src))
end

-- Don't move imports.lua: consumers name '@tLib/imports.lua' in their own
-- manifests, so the path is a contract.

shared_scripts {
    'shared/lib/adapter/init.lua',
    'shared/lib/logger.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/shim.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/core.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/events.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/ui.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/shutdown.lua',
    -- Before lifecycle.lua. Consumers load this exact file too.
    'shared/sh_branding.lua',
    -- The only definition of the studio API host. Consumers load it too.
    'shared/sh_api.lua',
    'shared/lib/adapter/lifecycle.lua',
    'shared/sh_utils.lua',
    'shared/sh_coords.lua',
    -- The menu protocol. Consumers validate against this exact file.
    'shared/lib/menu/schema.lua',
    -- Signatures must match byte for byte, so consumers run this file too.
    'shared/lib/menu/catalog.lua',
}

client_scripts {
    'client/lib/adapter/player.lua',
    'client/lib/adapter/vehicle.lua',
    'client/lib/adapter/world.lua',
    'client/cl_permission.lua',
    'client/lib/theme/exports.lua',
    'client/cl_theme.lua',
    -- Before cl_menu.lua, which hands it the resolver and publisher.
    'client/lib/menu/actions.lua',
    -- Always loaded: the menu client calls these, and they no-op if unused.
    'client/lib/menu/input.lua',
    -- After actions.lua: context walks every dispatcher on each pass.
    'client/lib/menu/context.lua',
    'client/lib/menu/prompts.lua',
    -- Last of the menu engine. Before cl_main.lua, which gives it the UI handle.
    'client/cl_menu.lua',
    'client/lib/toast/exports.lua',
    'client/cl_toast.lua',
    'client/cl_ui_effects.lua',
    'client/lib/dialog/state.lua',
    'client/lib/dialog/exports.lua',
    'client/cl_dialog.lua',
    'client/lib/layout/schema.lua',
    'client/cl_layout.lua',
    'client/cl_marketplace.lua',
    -- Before cl_main.lua, so ReportKeybind exists before consumers bind keys.
    'client/cl_keybinds.lua',
    'client/cl_main.lua',
}

server_scripts {
    'server/dist/bundle.js',
    -- Right after the bundle, whose absence or damage it exists to report.
    'server/sv_install.lua',
    'server/lib/adapter/utils.lua',
    'server/lib/adapter/permission.lua',
    -- Before sv_permission and sv_marketplace: in demo mode it overrides both.
    'server/sv_demo.lua',
    'server/sv_discovery.lua',
    -- The hub on the FiveM server port. After bundle.js, whose bridge exports the
    -- routing decision it asks for; a request before that is answered 503.
    'server/sv_http_ingress.lua',
    'server/sv_permission.lua',
    -- Server-only authority state. Before sv_menu.lua, which instantiates it.
    'server/lib/menu/registry.lua',
    -- Before sv_menu.lua, which dispatches `kind = 'feedback'` into it.
    'server/sv_feedback.lua',
    'server/sv_menu.lua',
    'server/sv_serversettings.lua',
    'server/sv_marketplace.lua',
    'server/sv_community_configs.lua',
    -- After sv_demo.lua, before sv_main.lua's boot handshake.
    'server/sv_telemetry.lua',
    'server/sv_main.lua',
}

files {
    'imports.lua',
    -- These two are read by consumers via LoadResourceFile.
    'shared/sh_branding.lua',
    'shared/sh_api.lua',
    'shared/imports/**/*.lua',
    'client/ui/index.html',
    'client/ui/assets/**/*',
}

ui_page 'client/ui/index.html'

if Bridge.Framework ~= 'qbcore' then return end

local QBCore = exports['qb-core']:GetCoreObject()

local function getPlayer(src)
    return QBCore.Functions.GetPlayer(src)
end

function Bridge.GetJob(src)
    local player = getPlayer(src)
    if not player then return end
    local job = player.PlayerData.job or {}
    local grade = job.grade or {}
    return job.name, tonumber(grade.level) or 0, job.onduty == true, job.label or job.name
end

function Bridge.GetCharName(src)
    local player = getPlayer(src)
    if not player then return Bridge.SplitName(GetPlayerName(src)) end
    local info = player.PlayerData.charinfo or {}
    return info.firstname or '', info.lastname or ''
end

local cache = nil

--- This will return the jobs registered in the framework in a table.
--- @return table<number, { name: string, label: string, grades: table<string, {name: string, label: string, grade: number }>}>
function GetFrameworkJobs()

    if cache then return cache end

    local jobs = {}

    if ESX then
        jobs = ESX.GetJobs()
    elseif QBCore then
        jobs = QBCore.Shared.Jobs
    elseif QBX then
        jobs = QBX:GetJobs()
    end

    for k, v in pairs(jobs) do
        jobs[k] = {
            name = v.name,
            label = v.label,
            grades = v.grades or {}
        }
    end

    cache = jobs
    return cache
end
